### Added: the reference AuthFetch client (#423)

`auth::clients::{AuthFetch, AuthFetchOptions, Response, parse_known_txids_header}`
adds the authenticated fetch client from `ts-stack@edf6e03`,
`packages/sdk/src/auth/clients/AuthFetch.ts` (all 1,300 lines read).
`AuthFetch::new(wallet, requested_certificates, session_manager)` shares one
wallet and session manager among per-origin Peers. `fetch(url, options)` returns
an owned `Response { status, headers, body }`; `send_certificate_request` requests
proofs and `consume_received_certificates` drains the most recent 1,000 proofs.
`AuthFetch`, its options and response are also re-exported from `auth`.
`AuthFetchOptions::payment_labels` exposes the reference label conversion.

The client is under `auth`; the existing `SimplifiedFetchTransport` needs native
`http`. An embedder can supply a transport factory under `auth` alone, including
the root's wasm slice. No runtime, thread or background task is started. Timers
use the Peer's existing native/wasm timeout helper; the 500 ms certificate grace
is a timer, not a thread sleep. Constructor builders configure an originator,
response deadline and body limit; `with_client` supplies a native HTTP client
(`auth::transports::NativeFetchClient` aliases that existing client type).
`with_max_response_bytes` configures the parser, the native transport from both
`new` and `with_client`, and fallback buffering. It also bounds the Peer's general
payload before the outgoing copy or incoming intake, to the greater of 16 MiB
and the response limit plus 512 KiB (clamped to the maximum safe integer), as
`:355-364` does. Changing the limit resets existing per-origin Peers. A custom
transport factory owns its I/O cap; the client still bounds its payload intake,
parser and native fallback. An injected HTTP client's redirect policy remains
the caller's. On wasm, `AuthFetch::new` compiles but every fetch is refused with
`HTTP transport requires the 'http' feature`; use `with_transport_factory`.

The reference sites and the corresponding behavior are:

- `:191-211`: wallet, optional requested certificates and sessions; `:342-398`
  creates one Peer per origin and registers certificate listeners. `:502-565`
  requests certificates with a 30-second deadline and keeps the latest 1,000.
- `:228-340`: decrement an explicitly supplied retry counter before any request,
  refuse zero, install the response listener before sending, and enforce the
  30-second default deadline. `:302-331,1066-1076` waits for the certificate queue;
  `:376-395` sends nonempty certificate responses and releases the queue only
  after the 500 ms grace, even when certificate work fails.
- `:400-426`: bounded stale-session recovery and unauthenticated fallback;
  `:680-705` rejects fallback responses claiming any `x-bsv*` header and rejects
  non-2xx statuses. The pinned transport's current handshake failure wording no
  longer triggers the legacy `HTTP server failed to authenticate` fallback arm;
  the recorder distinguishes this from the directly exercised fallback helper.
- `:572-674`: random 32-byte request ID, method, path, search, headers, body in
  that order. Header names are lowercased and sorted with the reference collation;
  authorization and `x-bsv-*` are supported, `x-bsv-auth*` is forbidden, and
  content-type parameters are stripped. POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE with no body use
  `{}` for application/json, otherwise the absent-body marker. Native options
  accept owned bytes: `None` is undefined, `Some(empty)` an empty typed array.
  JS FormData/Blob/ReadableStream and arbitrary object coercion have no Rust
  counterpart; callers serialize them first (`:1187-1243`). The transport body
  boundary requires Content-Type for nonempty bodies and validates text UTF-8.
- `:428-495,1246-1300`: bounded canonical CompactSize parsing; status 200–599,
  at most 512 headers, 1,024-byte names, 32,768-byte values, 262,144 total header
  bytes, configured body limit (16 MiB default), and 512 KiB frame overhead.
  The ID comparison at **`:439` ignores a nonmatching ID**, leaving the request
  pending until its matching response or deadline; it has no immediate mismatch
  refusal text. The successful response adds `x-bsv-auth-identity-key`.
- `:711-961`: BRC-105 version/amount/identity/prefix checks, wallet nonce suffix,
  protocol `[2, "3241645161d8"]`, key ID `prefix suffix`, P2PKH output, description
  `Payment for request to <origin>`, output description `HTTP request payment`,
  JSON custom instructions `derivationPrefix, derivationSuffix, payee`, and
  `randomizeOutputs: false`. The action includes
  `brc105 <hexPrefix> <hexSuffix>` followed by caller labels. The payment header
  JSON has `derivationPrefix, derivationSuffix, transaction` in that order.
  Compatible retries reuse the same payment; changed requirements recreate it.
  `:804-843,963-970,1134-1177` defaults retryCounter/payment attempts to three,
  waits `250 * min(attempt, 5)` ms after a paid failure, and bounds retries.
- `:131-150,745,905-910`: the optional `x-bsv-payment-known-txids` extension
  lowercases, filters to 64 hex digits, deduplicates in first-seen order, and
  takes at most 256 IDs for `createAction.options.knownTxids`. Invalid-only and
  absent headers leave the option absent. This is an SDK extension, not BRC-105.

The client creates `x-bsv-payment` on paid retries and adds the authenticated
identity to its returned headers. BRC-104 is the existing transport's HTTP
mapping: `x-bsv-auth-version`, `x-bsv-auth-identity-key`, `x-bsv-auth-nonce`,
`x-bsv-auth-your-nonce`, `x-bsv-auth-signature`, `x-bsv-auth-request-id`, and JSON
POSTs to `/.well-known/auth` with `Content-Type: application/json`. Incoming
`x-bsv-auth-message-type` / `x-bsv-auth-requested-certificates` select certificate
handling. BRC-103 supplies Peer authentication. Correlation, queueing, deadlines,
fallback and payment retries are the client's own behavior, not new BRC-104 wire
fields. The payment response headers are `x-bsv-payment-version`,
`x-bsv-payment-satoshis-required`, `x-bsv-payment-derivation-prefix`, plus the
optional known-txids extension above.

Refusal strings are retained inside `Error::AuthError` (its established Display
prefix remains). The client's fixed texts are:

- `Request failed after maximum number of retries.`
- `Authentication request capacity exceeded.`
- `Timed out waiting for authenticated response.`
- `Timeout waiting for certificate request to complete`
- `sendCertificateRequest timed out after 30000ms waiting for certificate response from <origin>`
- `Certificate response exceeds the per-message limit`
- `No BSV auth headers allowed here!`
- `Unsupported header in the simplified fetch implementation. Only content-type, authorization, and x-bsv-* headers are supported.`
- `The server is trying to claim it has been authenticated when it has not!`
- `Request failed with status: <status>`
- `Unsupported x-bsv-payment-version response header. Client version: 1.0, Server version: <version-or-null>`
- `Missing x-bsv-payment-satoshis-required response header.`
- `Invalid x-bsv-payment-satoshis-required response header value.`
- `Missing x-bsv-auth-identity-key response header.`
- `Missing x-bsv-payment-derivation-prefix response header.`
- `BRC-105 payment transaction must be a dense byte array of at most 16777216 bytes.`
- `Paid request to <origin> failed after <used>/<max> attempts. Sent <amount> satoshis to <identity>.`

The private payment cause `Maximum payment attempts exceeded before retrying`
and JavaScript error cause/stack/payment diagnostic objects (`:972-1185`) have
no fields in the crate's existing string error. This port emits no console log.
Body conversion's `ReadableStream cannot be directly converted to number[].`
and `Unsupported body type in this SimplifiedFetch implementation.` are excluded
by the typed byte-body API. The existing transport contributes
`Content-Type header is required for requests with a body.` and
`The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8`.

The new parser retains `Authenticated response frame exceeds the configured limit.`,
`Authenticated response contains an invalid HTTP status code.`,
`Authenticated response headers exceed the configured limit.`,
`Authenticated response body exceeds the configured limit.`,
`Authenticated response contains trailing bytes.`,
`Authenticated response truncated while reading <field>.`,
`Authenticated response contains an invalid <field>.`,
`non-canonical varInt`, `number too large to retain precision - use readVarIntBn`,
and `maxResponseBytes must be a positive safe integer`. Fields are `response nonce`,
`status code`, `response header count`, `response header name length`,
`response header name`, `response header value length`, `response header value`,
`response body length`, and `response body`. Fetch's header-name/value and
ByteString refusals and null-body status refusal are also recorded.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#423)

The cold-review fold conforms at three more reference sites:

- **Identity on ID match, conformed:** `AuthFetch.ts:428-452` commits the sender
  identity and mutual-auth flag after the frame bound and ID match, before
  parsing status, headers or body. Rust now does the same even if parsing refuses.
- **Content-Type trim, conformed:** `AuthFetch.ts:582-602` uses JavaScript trim.
  Rust now uses this crate's ECMAScript-trim helper, including U+FEFF and excluding
  U+0085, instead of `str::trim`.
- **Response header order, conformed:** the `Headers` constructed at
  `AuthFetch.ts:459-494` iterates names in sorted order. Both native response
  paths now expose that order through `Response.headers`.

The remaining departures are explicit:

- **STATED FINDING — 401 status:** `AuthFetch.ts:400-406` reads
  `error.details.status === 401`. This crate's existing `AuthError(String)` has
  no status field, so stale-session recovery matches `HTTP 401 ` together with
  `without valid BSV authentication` and an already-known peer identity.
- **STATED FINDING — native server-key parse:** `AuthFetch.ts:873-880` passes the
  server's key string to `wallet.getPublicKey`. Rust's typed `Counterparty::Other`
  requires a native `PublicKey` parse before that call; malformed keys therefore
  fail at this boundary, with native key-parser words, without calling the wallet.
- **STATED FINDING — timeout builder:** `AuthFetch.ts:90,298-300` fixes the
  response deadline at 30 seconds. `with_response_timeout_ms` is a Rust addition;
  its default remains 30 seconds, and it does not change certificate deadlines.
- **STATED FINDING — fallback cap:** `AuthFetch.ts:680-705` returns the plain
  `fetch` response after header/status validation without bounding its body.
  Rust buffers an owned body, so its own safeguard checks Content-Length and
  every streamed chunk against `max_response_bytes` before extending the buffer.
  It refuses with `Unauthenticated response from <url> exceeds <limit> bytes`.

`tests/auth_fetch_423_limits.rs` pins native limits below and above 16 MiB through
both constructors, the incoming/outgoing payload bounds and identity-on-match.
`tests/auth_fetch_423_fallback.rs` reads the recorded `fallback` handshake refusal
(an empty reason phrase) as well as the three direct helper cases: all 24 client
cases are exercised. Its fixed-length and chunked bodies read at eight bytes and
refuse at nine. The response-order and trim regressions are in
`tests/auth_fetch_423_response.rs` and `clients/request.rs`. Each changed behavior
was observed RED before this fold. The vector is unchanged; its one-file gitleaks
allowlist names the recorder's fixed test entropy and the cold review's two
byte-identical Node 22.18.0 runs.

The pin does **not** automatically replay an HTTP request after sending
certificates. Its `:392-394` only releases the queue. The HTTP fold also omits
`initialNonce`, which its Peer requires for a certificateRequest (#416):
`certificateRequest.initialNonce must be canonical base64.` The recorder and
Rust tests keep that full-intake refusal separate from the handler-only witness
and its **explicit** caller retry. No invented header or automatic replay is
added. Handshake-time certificate exchange is exercised without a bypass.

`Response` is a buffered native value, not a browser Fetch object: no stream,
statusText, URL, redirect metadata, JS body conversions or JS diagnostic objects.
The crate's collation profile and `Error` prefix remain the existing native
boundaries. Payment labels use the reference's permissive base64 conversion and its
padding/character refusal texts (`Invalid base64 padding` and
`Invalid base64 character at index <index>`), without altering nonce values on the wire.
The fetch retry counter is shared across nested paid attempts, including
backoff after a transport fault; cloning options cannot replenish it.

Go at `go-sdk@2ca481c`, `auth/clients/authhttp/authhttp.go`, has AuthFetch/New,
functional options (`:56-191`), context-based Fetch (`:194-548`), matching request
IDs before removing its listener (`:393-455`), certificate methods (`:550-652`),
and payment creation (`:703-827`). Its goroutines/context cancellation differ
from this port's awaited futures/timers; it updates peer identity before the ID
match, sends even empty certificate lists, releases the queue in a goroutine,
and returns a native `*http.Response`. Its payment action uses `auth-payment`
as originator, a full request URL description, and network lookup; it has no
caller labels, known-txids optimization, reused payment context or TS payment
backoff. Its errors are lowercase and often omit the TS punctuation. The
TypeScript client at the pin, rather than Go's surface or texts, is the authority.

`tests/support/auth_fetch_423.mjs` records the actual client, Peer and transport
under Node 22.18.0 with a fake fetch, fixed entropy, and accelerated deadlines;
only the explicitly labeled certificate-handler and fallback-helper witnesses
bypass their outer dispatch. `tests/vectors/auth_fetch_423.json` is recorder output
(two byte-identical runs). The six new `tests/auth_fetch_423*.rs` files cover
plain/correlated and mismatched answers, body defaults/bytes/refusals, timeout,
certificate queue/grace/intake/explicit retry/receive/drain, payment/reuse/labels/
known-txids/both exhausted budgets/header refusals, fallback, native limits and parser bounds.
Each file is RED on the base archive because the client module/API is absent;
request payloads are compared byte-for-byte after normalizing only request-ID
and payment-suffix entropy. `fuzz_auth_messages` now exercises the new response
parser (matching the ID to reach the rest) and known-txids parser.

### Added: certificate-response preimage witness across three SDKs (#375)

`tests/auth_certificate_preimage_375.rs` builds and signs two certificates
with deterministic test keys and IVs, then sends each through this crate's
`Peer::send_certificate_response` at the #400 signing site. The vector
`tests/vectors/auth_certificate_preimage_375.json` retains each certificate,
response, signed text, signature and all three signature-verification verdicts.
With fields/keyrings inserted as `zeta,alpha,10,2`, the reference and this
crate sign `2,10,zeta,alpha`; Go re-marshals `10,2,alpha,zeta` and rejects the
same signature. The byte-ordered `alpha,beta,gamma,zeta` control verifies in
all three. Rust also accepts both responses through its receiving Peer;
Node verifies and decrypts both certificates, and Go verifies both certificates.

The Node 22.18.0 recorder uses unmodified `ts-stack@edf6e03` built from a git
archive. The Go 1.27.0 recorder uses go-sdk v1.7.2 (`2ca481c`), a temporary
workspace replacement and the already populated module cache (`GOPROXY=off`;
no download). Each recorder's two runs are byte-identical. The foreign
recorders execute the Peer's certificate-response signature path through
`ProtoWallet.verifySignature` / `ProtoWallet.VerifySignature`, isolating it
from the separate nonce-handshake conventions; neither opens a port.
No library behavior changes. The Go draft is tenth, after the DER witness,
with its per-draft keeper word and the owner's cadence still pending; nothing
is filed. New divergence row 61 is accounted for under #400 below; later
current census row numbers move with the list, preserving historical prose.

### Added: a public typed input-word resolver (#520)

`script::Word::{Standard, Block}` and
`ChainParams::word_for_input(word: Word, spend_height: Option<u32>, source_height: Option<u32>) -> Result<ScriptFlags, NotJudgedCause>`
expose the existing private composition under the `script` and `block` features,
on the [keeper's 2026-10-30 18:12Z ruling](https://github.com/Calhooon/bsv-rs/issues/520#issuecomment-6530114599).
This is a semver-minor addition of public items (`cargo semver-checks --release-type minor`).
`Standard` is the live door's policy word; `Block` is the consensus word for a
mined transaction. `checked_input_script_flags` stays `pub(crate)`;
`input_script_flags` retains its signature, flags and error texts.

The no-tip rule is now inside the crate: a `None` spend height uses the latest
era the parameters know, `max(genesis_height, chronicle_height)`; an activation
is held back only for a named spend height that has not reached it. A `None`
source height is an unmined parent taking the spend's era. Transaction flags
follow the spend; only the two UTXO-era bits follow the source. The method's
docs cite the live door (`bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs@819dbcef`,
`src/storage/sqlx/beef_verification/live_word.rs:55-70`) and the inclusive era
table (`src/script/flags.rs:102-110`). The existing transaction and stream
verifiers now call the method for their standard word.

Migration for the toolbox: check tip + 1 and convert the proven source height
to `u32`, then call `chain.word_for_input(Word::Standard, spend_height, source_height)`;
delete `refusal_cause` and the mirrored activation/era order and no-tip fallback.
The resolver checks zero Genesis, zero Chronicle, pre-Genesis spend, then
pre-Genesis coin. Conversion refusals remain at the adapters. One existing
stream edge case differs from the issue's shorthand tip-first order: when both
the source and tip overflow, `SourceHeightOverflow` wins because the stream
converts its `u64` source first. That behavior is preserved and pinned.

`tests/script_word_for_input_520.rs` pins the public signature (compile-RED on
the base), 102 height/activation rows under both words against the legacy
selector, 97 rows expressible through each synchronous stream path, four
conversion-priority cases, and seven execution witnesses for independent
spend/coin era bits. Synthetic BEEF and BUMPs use the crate's writers.

### Added: per-transaction work budgets (#519)

`transaction::WorkBudget { per_input: Option<u64>, per_transaction: Option<u64> }`
is one local policy type for both bounds. Its adjacent `with_work_budget` and
`with_transaction_work_budget` builders (since #527, above, `with_per_input`
and `with_per_transaction`) set each bound independently; both
default to `None`. `StreamVerifier` and `AsyncStreamVerifier` retain their
existing `with_work_budget(Option<u64>)` and add the adjacent
`with_transaction_work_budget(Option<u64>)`. Whole-transaction callers pass the
type to `Transaction::verify_with_work_budgets` or
`verify_with_chain_params_and_work_budgets`; the existing singular methods and
their `Option<u64>` signatures remain available.

Each evaluated input's `Spend::work_spent()` is added after its evaluation, in
input order, to that transaction's running total. A total strictly above the
transaction bound stops verification before the next input with
`NotJudgedCause::TransactionWorkBudgetExceeded { input: u32, limit: u64, total: u64 }`:
the crossing input, the transaction limit, and the charged total including that
input. The crossing input runs under its per-input bound alone, so a refused
transaction's work is at most the limit plus one input's charge; with no
per-input bound that input is unbounded, and a door passes both. This is additive under `NotJudgedCause`'s existing `#[non_exhaustive]`.
The cause's Display is
`exceeded transaction work budget {limit} units after {total} units of work.`;
the existing wrappers still prefix the transaction and/or input once. `Error`
remains `Clone + PartialEq + Eq`, measured at 56 bytes on 64-bit targets;
`NotJudgedCause` remains 24 bytes.

`StreamVerifier::work_spent()` and `AsyncStreamVerifier::work_spent()` expose
the current or most recently evaluated transaction's running total, including
work before a refusal. A transaction-budget `Verdict::NotJudged` exposes the
total in its cause and through `Verdict::work_spent() -> Option<u64>`; other
verdicts have no stored total and return `None`. Accepted totals remain available
on the stream verifier. The existing whole-transaction `Result<bool>` and
verdict variant fields are unchanged. Totals reset for each unproven
transaction, including ancestors and deferred transactions. A proof or
structure-only read spends no work. A transaction-only bound enables the same
interpreter accounting; existing per-input, memory and script refusals keep
their classes. Counters saturate at `u64::MAX`; overflow also exceeds a
configured transaction bound, so wrapping cannot admit work.

Local limits remain absent from cursors and must be reapplied after resume.
Metered cursors use BSC5 to retain the transaction and total already charged,
including pauses in deferred transactions. BSC2/BSC3/BSC4 remain readable and
unmetered cursors retain their bytes. Applying a budget to an old or unmetered
cursor replays the transaction prefix so prior work cannot evade its bound.

Migration for the toolbox: **delete the door-side sum and pass the transaction
limit** alongside the per-input limit, both `Some(1 << 31)` under its current
policy. The sum described in toolbox #487 and bsv-rs #519 is now owned by this
verifier. The keeper's [2026-10-30 18:12Z ruling](https://github.com/Calhooon/bsv-rs/issues/519#issuecomment-6530114206)
sets the two-bound type, the cause's fields and the minor-release classification.

| Consumer table | Before | New not-judged cause and migration |
|---|---|---|
| Toolbox doors and signer | `WorkBudgetExceeded { input, budget, work_done }` per input; doors sum input work themselves | Keep the per-input row; add `TransactionWorkBudgetExceeded { input, limit, total }`, delete the sum, and pass the transaction limit. No invalid-transaction verdict is implied. |
| CLI verification/error table | Existing scope and per-input work causes, wildcard for future causes | Add the transaction-work row, showing the crossing input, limit and total. Its Display uses the sentence above, through the existing `TransactionNotJudged`/`NotJudged` wrappers. |

`tests/transaction_work_budget_519.rs` pins the 68/6/8-unit inputs crossing 70
at input 1 with total 74, exact/ample bounds, independent limits, refusal
precedence, accounting without a per-input bound, cursor round trips, ancestors,
deferred ordering and unchanged error sizes. The beta.4 reproduction returned
`Ok(true)` and `Valid` with every input green. The existing #378 witnesses also
remain unchanged.

The transaction-parser fuzz target also parses and rewrites cursors, covering
the BSC5 accounting state with the required parser run.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#519)

This is the keeper's local evaluator policy, not a new consensus rule or an
elapsed-time bound. The reference's `Transaction.verify` has only the optional

### Fixed: require documentation before landing and skip tag benchmark comparisons (#515)

The first beta.4 [Release run](https://github.com/Calhooon/bsv-rs/actions/runs/41058300024)
failed rustdoc on an unresolved intra-doc link that had passed two reviewed PRs:
`Documentation` was absent from their required set. On the keeper's 2026-10-30
13:2xZ word, the job moves from `docs.yml` back into `ci.yml`, whose triggers
include pull requests and pushes to both lines. Its command stays
`cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` under `RUSTDOCFLAGS: -Dwarnings`.
`Documentation` joins `REQUIRED_ON_BETA` and `REQUIRED_ON_MAIN`;
`docs.yml` retains actionlint. The constants describe the intended protection
after landing, not the current settings: the captain must add `Documentation`
to `beta`'s protection when this lands on `beta`, and to `main`'s only when
`main`'s `ci.yml` carries the job (its cherry-pick; before that no run into
`main` reports the context and every pull request there would wait on it),
reading each back, then update the sequencer's required-check list.

The third beta.4 [Release run](https://github.com/Calhooon/bsv-rs/actions/runs/41076363406)
published successfully but concluded failure on benchmark comparisons, reporting
`FAIL (9 of 9 benches measured)` against the +5% p99 threshold, including
nanosecond-scale wire-codec measurements.
Its job list names `Bench / Benchmark Regression Check`: the job had moved to
`bench.yml` and had no event guard there. The PR-only guard reported for
`ci.yml` was not the running job. A reusable workflow reads its caller's
event and ref ([GitHub's caller context](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/reusing-workflow-configurations#github-context)),
so the Release call is a tag push, with empty PR refs.
The comparison job now rejects `refs/tags/` through `github.ref`, including
manual dispatches of a tag; branch dispatches and PR callers remain allowed
by the guard. Beta's existing dispatch/call-only benchmark triggers remain,
as do tag benchmark builds and the scoreboard. No baselines or thresholds
change. Architecture tests prove the docs job runs for PRs and pushes and
that tag callers skip comparisons without disabling branch dispatches.

### Changed: `WorkBudget` is `#[non_exhaustive]` with a constructor and field setters (#527)

`transaction::WorkBudget` previously allowed downstream struct literals, so
adding a third bound would break every such consumer. The keeper's
2026-10-30 20:1xZ word for 0.9.0-beta.5 seals that shape now:
`#[non_exhaustive]` with both fields still public and readable, a const
`new()` with both bounds `None`, and const, `#[must_use]` `with_per_input` and
`with_per_transaction` setters taking `Option<u64>`. Derived `Default` equals
`new()`; the existing accounting and verifier behavior are unchanged.

Migration: `WorkBudget { per_input: a, per_transaction: b }` becomes
`WorkBudget::new().with_per_input(a).with_per_transaction(b)`; a destructure
outside the crate takes `..`. On `WorkBudget`, `with_work_budget` and
`with_transaction_work_budget` are replaced by `with_per_input` and
`with_per_transaction`, with no aliases. The verifier builders keep their
names and signatures.

This is a semver-major change on the beta line under `api-break`.
`WorkBudget` is in no published prerelease: it arrived in #519 (`77cccd70`),
after v0.9.0-beta.4 (`56d12075`). The struct's `compile_fail` doctest pins the
external literal's rejection; `tests/transaction_work_budget_519.rs` pins
`a_new_work_budget_matches_the_unbounded_default_527`,
`work_budget_field_setters_keep_both_bounds_readable_527`, and
`work_budget_construction_and_both_field_setters_are_const_527`.
Each was RED on the pre-fix base. The literal in
`tests/transaction_work_budget_519.rs` now uses the constructor and setters;
all #519 assertions retain their meaning.

### Changed: the local store decodes lock-before alone, as the reference does (#499)

The keeper's word (2026-10-30 05:1xZ, issue #499): lock-before alone, as the
reference decodes it. At `ts-stack@edf6e03` the local lookup decodes a token
with `decodeCanonicalPushDrop` (`LocalKVStore.ts:278-282`), which calls
`PushDrop.decode(lockingScript)` with its default `lockPosition = 'before'`
(`PushDropValidation.ts:59`, `PushDrop.ts:63-77`): the first chunk's data
(`verifyNotNull(..., 'script.chunks[0].data must have value')`) is read as the
key by `PublicKey.fromString` before any field is counted. This crate's local
decode called the general `PushDrop::decode`, which reads a script whose first
chunk is not a 33- or 65-byte push as lock-after, so a lock-after token
reached the later field-count or canonical-envelope check and told another
refusal than the reference's. `local_parser_words.rs::decode_pushdrop` now
reads the first chunk as the reference does and never the lock-after layout;
the refusal is the reference's first-chunk words, `Error::KvStoreLocalError`
in the lookup wrapper (`Invalid value found. Relinquish the corrupted output
from the kvstore basket before using this key again. Original error: <words>`,
`LocalKVStore.ts:340-345`), on get and set alike.

| Token (`<G>` the generator's compressed push) | Before (#489's stated row) | Now, the reference's |
|---|---|---|
| `51 75 <G> ac` | `Unexpected PushDrop token field count` | `script.chunks[0].data must have value` |
| `51 52 6d <G> ac` | `PushDrop token must use the canonical PushDrop envelope` | `script.chunks[0].data must have value` |
| `00 75 <G> ac` | `Unexpected PushDrop token field count` | `script.chunks[0].data must have value` |
| `01 07 75 <G> ac` | `Unexpected PushDrop token field count` | `Unknown point format` |
| `02 07 08 01 09 6d <G> ac` | `PushDrop token must use the canonical PushDrop envelope` | `Unknown point format` |
| `51 52 6d <04 Gx Gy> ac` | `PushDrop token must use the canonical PushDrop envelope` | `script.chunks[0].data must have value` |

The #489 entry's note that `00 75 <G> ac` gets `Unknown point format` in the
reference was wrong: `OP_0` carries no data there, so the reference says
`script.chunks[0].data must have value`, as recorded. The words are recorded,
never written by hand: the #326 recorder's `--kvstore-local-454` mode
(`tests/support/signaction_reference_326.mjs` through
`tests/support/kvstore_local_parser_words_489.mjs`, the bundle of
`ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0) now writes the six shapes as kind
`token_lock_after` for get and set into `tests/vectors/kvstore_local_454.json`
(`parser_words_489`, 52 cases to 60: the two #489 lock-after inputs lose their
`parser_accepted` flag and four are new); every other field of the vector is
byte for byte unchanged, and the recorder reproduced the base vector byte for
byte before the extension. `a_lock_after_token_is_refused_by_the_reference_lock_before_read_499`
in `tests/kvstore_local_parser_words_489.rs` replaces #489's two lock-after
pins and asserts the port's words equal the vector's for all twelve cases; it
was red on `aa5d60db` (`Unexpected PushDrop token field count` for the first).

The general `PushDrop::decode` and its lock-after path are unchanged (the test
asserts each shape still decodes there as lock-after). Every reference call of
`PushDrop.decode` under `packages/sdk/src` at `edf6e03` takes the lock-before
default (`PushDropValidation.ts:59`, reached from the kvstore, registry,
overlay admin token and UHRP validators; `ContactsManager.ts:432`;
`IdentityClient.ts:773`) and none passes `'after'`; this crate's identity,
registry, kvstore interpreter, overlay admin token and storage call sites keep
the general decoder's detection, a question for a second issue, not this one.
No public API, acceptance of a valid token or other error text changes.

### Changed: R56 lets an unsigned action's input carry no unlockingScript, as the reference wallet answers (#491)

R56 (`src/wallet/substrates/result_values/lists.rs`, `action_inputs` through
`unlocking_requested`), the listActions input row of #432's result inventory,
demanded `unlockingScript` under `includeInputUnlockingScripts` on every input.
It now lets an input of an action whose `status` is exactly `unsigned` omit the
key; every other status keeps the demand in the same words. The status is read
from the action object the input belongs to. Nothing else in R56, or in any
other row, changes: a present `unlockingScript` must still be even hex, and the
`sourceLockingScript` demand under `includeInputSourceLockingScripts` is
unchanged for every status.

The word is the stack's (the keeper, 2026-10-31 05:1xZ, recorded on #491):
form (a) in its narrow reading, at `ts-stack@edf6e03`. The reference disagrees
with itself. Its wallet leaves the key absent when
`getRawTxOfKnownValidTransaction` returns nothing
(`packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox/src/storage/methods/listActionsIdb.ts:77-91`:
`wo.unlockingScript = input?.unlockingScript?.toHex()`). That holds outside
the known-valid set, a `proven_txs` row or a `proven_tx_reqs` row with status
unsent, unmined, unconfirmed, sending, nosend or completed
(`packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox/src/storage/StorageKnex.ts:189-209`). An
unsigned transaction is outside that set and holds no unlocking script. Its
SDK refuses any such page (`packages/sdk/src/wallet/WalletResultValidation.ts:2027-2035`),
and runs that validator on every answer (`packages/sdk/src/wallet/WalletClient.ts:113-118`).
The defect is ts-stack #1451 (open). Only the `unsigned` status is decidable
from the answer: an action's status and a request row's status are different
enumerations, so whether a signed action's transaction is known valid is a
storage fact the answer does not show, and projecting it onto the answer would
be this crate's invention.

The toolbox's and CLI's tables change as follows:

| Consumer | Answer under `includeInputUnlockingScripts` | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Toolbox result table | An `unsigned` action's input without `unlockingScript` (`transactions.rs:420-426`, the reference wallet's line) | Refused: `Invalid listActions result actions[N].inputs[M].unlockingScript: expected the explicitly requested unlocking script` | Accepted |
| Toolbox result table | An input without `unlockingScript` of an action with status completed, unprocessed, sending, unproven, nosend, nonfinal or failed | Refused in those words | Refused in those words (unchanged) |
| CLI operator-visible table | Fixture 145 (`pin-spend`, the stored unsigned template's input) | Refused by R56 | Passes R56; refused by R51 instead, its one-byte `inputDescription` `"c"` outside 5 to 2000 bytes (`Invalid listActions result actions[5].inputs[0].inputDescription: expected 5–2000 UTF-8 bytes`), a rule the reference's validator also applies (`historyDescription`, after its R56 check) |
| Both | An `unsigned` action's input with an `unlockingScript` | Validated as even hex | Validated as even hex (unchanged) |

The residue row [D]: a signed action with status unprocessed, nonfinal or
failed stays strict here, though the reference wallet answers its input
without the key when the request row is outside the known-valid set. It stays
until ts-stack #1451 answers. If the validator is amended upstream, this crate
follows the amended text; if the wallet is amended to emit the key, R56 returns
to strict for `unsigned` too and the toolbox's `transactions.rs:420` follows
the wallet.

Fixture 145's description: the CLI's fixture carries `inputDescription: "c"`,
which R51 refuses on both sides; R56 ran first, so its refusal was the only
one seen. This change does not make fixture 145 pass. The cold review ran the
recorded body (`bsv-wallet-cli` beta `c1f7cd3`,
`tests/wire/145-listActions.afterOverlongSpend.json`) through both: this crate

whose first chunk is not a 33- or 65-byte push as lock-after: a token written
lock-after was read here and refused by every counterpart. The keeper's word
(2026-10-31 06:1xZ, issue #537): parity per site. `PushDrop.decode(script,
lockPosition = 'before')` (`ts-stack@edf6e03` `PushDrop.ts:63-78`) reads the
key from `chunks[0]` and never tries the other position, and each
counterpart below calls it with that default (or through
`decodeCanonicalPushDrop`, `PushDropValidation.ts:59`); none passes
`'after'`. Each site now calls `PushDrop::decode_before`, the lock-before
path alone (crate-visible, `src/script/templates/pushdrop_position.rs`), and
takes the reference's outcome for a lock-after token there.

| Site (this crate) | Reference counterpart | Lock-after token, before | Now | The corner: a lock-after token whose first field is a valid point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 identity client: both `ls_identity` parsers (`resolve_by_identity_key`, `resolve_by_attributes`, `discover_certificates`, `discover_certificates_by_type`) | `IdentityClient.ts:773`, the output skipped by the catch at `:823` | the certificate read and returned | skipped | the reference reads the point as the key, one field, `continue` at `:774` (its revocation ends `No authenticated revelation output matches the requested certificate.`); skipped here before and after |

| 4 kvstore interpreter: `extract_fields`, `extract_value`, `is_kvstore_token` | `kvStoreTokenValidation.ts:88`, `undefined` from `kvStoreInterpreter.ts:48` | fields and value read, `true` | `None`, `None`, `false` | `Unexpected PushDrop token field count` there; `None`/`false` here before and after |

### Changed: `PublicKey::from_hex` accepts the reference's lenient forms (#498)

The keeper's word (2026-10-30 05:1xZ, on #498, under the reading of record
of 10-26): accept what the reference accepts, refuse what the standard
forbids and the reference refuses, the question upstream, the pinned tests
kept so strictness can return. A key the reference reads and this crate
refused was two verdicts for one user. `PublicKey::from_hex` now reads a
key string as
`PublicKey.fromString` does at `ts-stack@edf6e03` (`PublicKey.ts:49-51`,
`Point.fromString` at `Point.ts:345-348`), one parser
(`src/primitives/ec/public_key_forms.rs`):

| Form | Before | Now | The reference's site |
|---|---|---|---|
| An odd-length string (`2`+Gx, `3`+Gx, `4`+Gx+Gy, `6`+Gx+Gy, `7`+Gx+y) | `invalid hex string: Odd number of digits` | read with a leading `0` | `utils.ts:127-128` (`hexToUint8Array`; the rule of `hex.ts:27-29`) |
| A hybrid key (`06`/`07` + x + y) whose prefix's low bit is y's last byte's | `invalid public key: Invalid public key encoding: elliptic curve point encoding error` | accepted | `Point.ts:305-321` |
| A coordinate at or above p: a compressed x (`02`+(p+1)), an uncompressed or hybrid x or y (`04`+(p+1)+y) | `invalid public key: Point not on curve` (compressed), the encoding error (uncompressed, hybrid) | reduced modulo p | `Point.ts:365-384` (`fromX`), `:495-510` (`validate`) |

Every refusal the reference makes stays a refusal, in this crate's class and

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#498)

The ecosystem is split; the reference is the most tolerant reader. Each form
read by `PublicKey.fromString` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`), go-sdk's
`PublicKeyFromString` (`2ca481c`, `primitives/ec/publickey.go:79-129,221-231`)
and py-sdk's `PublicKey(str)` (`4c30e2e`, `bsv/keys.py:23-45`, coincurve
20.0.0's libsecp256k1 parse), each run on the vector's inputs:

| Form | TS | Go | Python | This crate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Odd-length string | accepts | refuses (`encoding/hex: odd length hex string`) | refuses (`bytes.fromhex`) | accepts |
| Hybrid, matching parity | accepts | accepts | accepts | accepts |
| Hybrid, wrong parity | refuses | refuses | refuses | refuses |
| Compressed x at or above p | accepts, reduced | accepts, x kept unreduced (`Compressed()` writes `02`+(p+1) back) | refuses | accepts, reduced |
| Uncompressed or hybrid x or y at or above p | accepts; `toString` writes the coordinate unreduced, its compressed prefix from y's unreduced parity (`04`+x+(p+1) reads as y = 1 and writes `02`+x, the negated point) | refuses (`pubkey X/Y parameter is >= to P`) | refuses | accepts, reduced; writes the point read (`03`+x) |

Two differences remain. The reference's serialization of an uncompressed or
hybrid key with a coordinate at or above p differs from this crate's (five
recorded cases, `the_reference_writes_an_unreduced_coordinate_back_498`; for
a y above p the reference's compressed text names the other point: for
`04`+x+(p+1) it computes with y = 1 and writes `02`+x, the negated point,
where this crate writes `03`+x, the point read; that `02`+x is the
reference's defect, never parity, by the keeper's word of 2026-10-31 06:1xZ
(`Point.ts:303-321,472-478,527-536`; a FILE draft in the #375 queue, filed at
the owner's cadence word), and a leading space is read
by Python's `bytes.fromhex` alone. Strictness returns on the upstream's
answer: `PublicKey::from_bytes` is the strict reading, and flipping the
pins back is the change. Ours: the keeper's 2026-10-30 05:1xZ word on #498 accepts the reference's key forms on the hex path (Point.ts:303-325,365-384 at edf6e03), while BRC-100 at 5119a9b wallet/0100.md defines PubKeyHex as compressed and the byte path stays strict.

### Fixed: the contacts manager uses the reference's contact protocol (#542)

The contacts manager derived every contact key at security level 1:
`Protocol::new(SecurityLevel::App, "contact")`, `[1, 'contact']`, at four
sites, while `ContactsManagerConfig::protocol_id` held `(2, "contact")` and
went unread. The reference uses `[2, 'contact']`, counterparty `'self'`, for
every contact operation (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/identity/ContactsManager.ts:30`). Each site now reads the
protocol from the configuration (`ContactsManager::protocol`, private), so the
default is the reference's `[2, 'contact']`:

| Site (this crate) | Wallet call | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| `contacts.rs`, `create_identity_tag` | createHmac over the identity key, key ID the identity key (the lookup and output tag) | `#hashIdentityKey`, `:572-583` |
| `contacts_actions.rs`, `contact_lock` | encrypt, then getPublicKey `forSelf` for the PushDrop lock, key ID the record's | `#encryptAndLock`, `:748-772` |
| `contacts_actions.rs`, `contact_unlock` | the PushDrop spend's createSignature, the stored key ID | `#updateContactOutput`, `:821-830` |
| `contacts_cache.rs`, `decode_cached_contact` | decrypt, the stored key ID | `#decryptContactOutputs`, `:494-501` |

Before, level 1 against the reference's level 2 at every site: the
reference's contact record did not decrypt here (dropped from
`list_contacts_with_refresh`), this crate's ciphertext did not decrypt there
(`Decryption failed!`), the token was locked to another key, the identity tag
was another HMAC (so neither side's lookup by tag found the other's record),
and a spend of the reference's token was signed by a key its lock does not
name. Now the records are readable across implementations at the protocol:
the reference's record is read here, and this crate's ciphertext is decrypted
by the reference's wallet under `[2, 'contact']`. The keeper's reading
(2026-10-31 07:1xZ, issue #542): a cross-implementation incompatibility, a
parity row at the pin. The toolbox has no contacts path; the CLI's tables are
unchanged. No public item changes; a caller who set `protocol_id` now gets
the level it set (it was ignored before).

The witness is recorded, never written by hand:
`tests/support/contacts_protocol_542.mjs` runs the reference's own
`ContactsManager.saveContact` (the bundle of `ts-stack@edf6e03`, an entry
re-exporting `ContactsManager`, under Node v22.18.0, the ProtoWallet of the
scalar 9, #310's randomness) and reads back with its `getContacts`; it takes
this crate's token from the base and the tip as input (written by the ignored
`record_this_crates_contact_token_542`) and records the reference's verdicts on
them, in `tests/vectors/contacts_protocol_542.json` (two runs byte for byte).
`tests/identity_contacts_protocol_542.rs`: the reference's record read here,
the identity tag the reference's HMAC, this crate's token locked to the key the
reference derives and its ciphertext decrypted under the reference's protocol,
the spend of the reference's token verified under the reference's lock, each
red on `b51cbea7`; the reference's recorded verdicts on the base's token
(another key, `Decryption failed!`) and the tip's (its key, the record
decrypted).

### Notes: cross-SDK parity

The reference's `ContactsManager` still drops this crate's token, on the base

The registry client read and wrote a definition token of 6, 6 and 7 fields
(basket, protocol, certificate: the data fields, the operator's identity key
last), unsigned, locked with the operator's identity key. The reference's
token carries one more field, the operator's signature over the data fields,
and is locked with the operator's key linked to `anyone`
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `RegistryClient.ts:308-342`, `:688-722`;
`PushDrop.ts:146-202`). A token written here was refused by the reference's
validator (`Unexpected PushDrop token field count`), and the reference's
token was skipped here by the field count. The keeper's reading (2026-10-31
07:1xZ, recorded on #543): a parse divergence that dropped the reference's
signature from the record; a parity row at the pin, the second of three
after #537.

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Script fields (basket / protocol / certificate) | 6 / 6 / 7 | 7 / 7 / 8: the same data fields, then the signature (`registryTokenValidation.ts:13-17,29`) |
| Signature | none | the wallet's `createSignature` over the data fields' bytes concatenated, protocol `[1, basketmap]`, `[1, protomap]` or `[1, certmap]`, key ID `1`, counterparty `anyone` (`PushDrop.ts:173-185`) |
| Locking key | the identity key | the wallet's `getPublicKey` for the same protocol and key ID, counterparty `anyone`, `forSelf` true (`RegistryClient.ts:320`, `PushDrop.ts:155-163`) |

| `DefinitionType::expected_field_count` | 6 / 6 / 7 | 7 / 7 / 8, the script's count as its documentation says |

### Fixed: a SEC 1 tag 05 is refused as the reference refuses it (#550)

k256 (sec1 0.8.1, `src/point.rs:521-533`) reads a SEC 1 tag `05` as a compact
point, so `PublicKey::from_bytes(05 || Gx)` returned the key `02 || Gx`, and
every site that reads a key through `from_bytes` without a prefix check took
the compact form as a key. The reference's `Point.fromDER` reads the prefixes
`02`, `03`, `04`, `06`, `07` and refuses every other as `Unknown point format`
(`ts-stack@edf6e03` `Point.ts:303-325`). `from_bytes` now refuses a `05` tag
before k256 reads it, as `Error::InvalidPublicKey("Invalid public key encoding:
unknown point format")`, the words `from_hex`'s lenient parser (#498,
`src/primitives/ec/public_key_forms.rs`) already used for every shape the
reference does not read; `from_hex` refused `05` on the base already (its
`unknown point format` arm; `public_key_forms_498.json` records the reference
refusing `compressed_prefix_05` and `compact_prefix_05_odd_length`), unchanged.
Other tags k256 refuses keep k256's words.

| Site | Before (base `69d315fc`) | Now | The reference (`ts-stack@edf6e03`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PublicKey::from_bytes` | `05 \|\| Gx` read as `02 \|\| Gx` | refused, `InvalidPublicKey` | `Unknown point format` |
| `PublicKey::from_hex` | refused (#498) | unchanged | `Unknown point format` |
| `PushDrop::decode`, both positions (`pushdrop.rs:289,335`) | the token read with the compact key | refused, `InvalidPublicKey` | `PushDrop.decode`: `Unknown point format` |
| The kvstore token reader and interpreter (`kvstore/token_validation.rs`, #544) | a `05` locking key: `PushDrop token must use the canonical PushDrop envelope`; a `05` controller field: read as the compact key, so a token signed by `02 \|\| x` read to its value | `Unknown point format` for both (`point_message` at the controller, as `validateKVStoreController` reads it, `kvStoreTokenValidation.ts:76-81`); no value | the same words; no value |
| `KVStoreInterpreter::verify_signature` (`interpreter.rs:168`) | `true` for that token | `false` | (its reader refuses the controller) |
| `messages::verify`, the signer (`signed.rs:170`) | read as the compact key: `Ok(true)` on the recorded message | refused, `InvalidPublicKey` | `Unknown point format` |
| `messages::verify` and `messages::decrypt`, the recipient (`signed.rs:205`, `encrypted.rs:184`) | parsed, then compared as keys: a mismatch naming `02 \|\| x` (or a match when the recipient's key is `02 \|\| x`) | the bytes compared with the recipient's compressed key, as the reference compares their hex (`SignedMessage.ts:85-97`, `EncryptedMessage.ts:88-94`): `MessageRecipientMismatch` naming the `05` bytes | the mismatch naming the `05` bytes |
| `messages::decrypt`, the sender (`encrypted.rs:177`) | decrypted | refused, `InvalidPublicKey` | `Unknown point format` |
| `Certificate::from_binary`, subject and certifier | parsed | refused, `InvalidPublicKey` | `Invalid certificate subject` (`certifier`)`: expected a compressed secp256k1 public key` |
| `compat::ecies::bitcore_decrypt`, the sender | decrypted | refused, `InvalidPublicKey` | `Unknown point format` |
| The wire processor's counterparty (`wallet/wire/encoding.rs:165`) | getPublicKey answered with a key derived for the compact point | a key whose tag is not `02`/`03` is `#decodeCounterparty`'s `Point.fromDER` (`WalletWireProcessor.ts:2459-2460`): the error frame `01`, `Unknown point format`, an empty stack, byte for byte | the same frame |
| `validate_requested_certificate_set`, a certifier text | accepted | refused, `Certifier '05…' is not a valid public key` | (this crate's checker; the `Peer` does not call it) |

Guarded already and unchanged: the script interpreter

### Fixed: the registry client unlocks a definition token as the reference does on revoke and update (#548)

`revoke_own_registry_entry` and `update_definition` answered the wallet's
signable transaction with an empty unlocking script for the definition
token's input, keyed by the token's output index, not its input index in
the transaction (`src/registry/client.rs:653`, `:877` at `69d315fc`). The
reference unlocks the token with `PushDrop.unlock(protocol, '1', 'anyone',
'all', false, satoshis, lockingScript)` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`RegistryClient.ts:540-548` for `removeDefinition`, `:630-639` for
`updateDefinition`; `PushDrop.ts:217-262`): the BIP-143 preimage under
SIGHASH_ALL | FORKID over the authenticated record's satoshis and locking
script, its SHA-256 signed by the wallet's `createSignature` under the
type's protocol (`[1, basketmap|protomap|certmap]`), key ID `1`,
counterparty `anyone`, one push of the checksig signature, at the token's
index in the signable transaction (`completeBoundAction`). Since #543 the
token is locked with the operator's `anyone`-linked key, which only that
signature opens. Both sites now build the spend through the one PushDrop
signer the key-value stores and the identity client use
(`wallet::pushdrop::sign`, now compiled under `registry` too), from
`src/registry/unlock.rs`: the token's input found in the signable
transaction by its outpoint, the createAction input still declaring
`unlockingScriptLength: 74` as the reference's does. Their signAction now
carries the signable transaction's `reference` as the base64 text the
wallet answered (`to_base64`, as the key-value stores and the contacts
manager send it; `completeBoundAction.ts:1044-1051`, `:1118`, BRC-100's
`Base64String`), where it sent the UTF-8 reading of its bytes
(`String::from_utf8(..).unwrap_or_default()`, `src/registry/client.rs:657`,
`:877` at `20b0fcae`): an empty text for bytes that are not UTF-8, another
reference for bytes that are, so no wallet found the action to sign.

For the toolbox's and the CLI's tables: a revoke or an update built by this
crate before this landing did not spend the definition token: its input
carried an empty unlocking script (at the wrong index when the wallet put
the token anywhere but at its own output index), which does not satisfy the
token's lock, so the revocation or update was not a valid spend unless the
wallet replaced the script itself; one built now carries the reference's
script.

The witness is recorded, never written by hand:
`tests/support/registry_unlocking_548.mjs` runs the reference's own
`registerDefinition`, `removeDefinition` and `updateDefinition` (the bundle
of `ts-stack@edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0) with a `ProtoWallet` of the
scalar 9 for each definition type, its createAction answered with a
signable transaction spending a made-up funding input at index 0 and the
token at index 1, its signAction recorded and answered with no transaction;
`tests/vectors/registry_unlocking_548.json` holds six cases (basket,
protocol, certificate; revoke, update): the signable transaction, the spend

The `ProtoWallet`'s signatures are RFC 6979's, deterministic, so the bytes

the token's output index (`registry/methods.go:416-441`), right only when the

### Fixed: Contact carries the reference's badge fields through read and write (#552)

The reference's contact record carries three badge fields beside its name
and keys: `validateContact` (`ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/identity/ContactsManager.ts:171-192`) takes every one of
the seven display fields (`:35-43`) through `ownData` (`:47-53`, a missing
key refused as `must be an own data property`) and then its validator
(`:75`, a non-string refused), so a record the reference reads carries
`badgeIconURL`, `badgeLabel` and `badgeClickURL` as strings, empty where
unset. After #544 this crate wrote and read that record, but its `Contact`
had no badge members: a reference contact's badges were dropped on read,
every save wrote them empty, and a round trip through this crate's update
(read, change the name, save) erased the badges the reference had stored.
The keeper's reading (2026-10-31 12:1xZ, issue #552): a user's data lost on
an update, a parity row at the pin.

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Read (`list_contacts_with_refresh`, `contact_of`) | the three badge values read, validated and dropped | kept in `Contact::badge_icon_url`, `badge_label`, `badge_click_url` |
| Write (`add_contact`, `update_contact`, `record_of`) | `badgeIconURL`, `badgeLabel`, `badgeClickURL` written `""` | written as the `Contact` holds them, `""` where unset, as the reference writes them |
| A reference contact updated here | its badges erased in the token written | its badges kept; the reference reads back the record it wrote with the new name |

For the toolbox's and the CLI's tables: the toolbox has no contacts path and
the CLI none, so neither table changes.

`tests/support/contact_badges_552.mjs` runs the reference's own
`ContactsManager` (the bundle of `ts-stack@edf6e03`, an entry re-exporting
it, under Node v22.18.0, the ProtoWallet of the scalar 9 in process, a
SHA-256 counter stream for its randomness): `saveContact` of a contact with
the three badges set, its token, plaintext and `getContacts` read-back; it
takes this crate's tokens from the tip and the base as input (written by the

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#375)

Go verifies the low-S and high-S inputs and both converted certificates,
but its adapter rewrites high S to low S (`certificate.go:274-280,319-322`,
`signature.go:77-102,297-299`). TypeScript and this crate preserve both
accepted signatures. TypeScript `Certificate.ts:309-311,395-397,425-439`
parses and writes/re-encodes DER; `Signature.ts:201-247` preserves S, and
`ECDSA.ts:236-239` accepts either S form. The BER length probe is refused
by both parsers (`signature.go:199-207`, `Signature.ts:45-51`); Go's adapter
drops its signature and returns an unsigned certificate. This refusal
control is not the draft's claim. BRC-52 at `5119a9b`,
`peer-to-peer/0052.md:93,103`, specifies DER and recommends retaining
signature bytes without requiring low S; BRC-53 `wallet/0053.md:13-15`
defers current certificate behavior to BRC-52/100. Nothing has been filed.

### Added: a default-mode fuzz target for the script interpreter (#398)

`fuzz_script_spend` picks a node word from its first byte, so every input ran
under `ScriptFlags::block` or `standard` and the default mode (no `set_flags`,
the TypeScript reference's verdicts) was never fuzzed: over its 678 seeds the
word target makes 681 evaluations, 0 of them in the default mode, on the base
`faa2c97e` and on this tip. `fuzz_script_spend_default`, a sibling `[[bin]]`,
evaluates `Spend` without a word under the same work budget, counting allocator
and bounds, now one module both targets include (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/spend/`):
687 default-mode evaluations over its seeds. A sibling and not a first-byte
value of the word target: the word target's corpus keeps every entry's meaning,
and the default mode has its own hour in the nightly rather than a share of
the word target's.

The input is the word target's layout (byte 0's bit 2 the version, bytes 1-2
the unlocking length), so its seeds are the word target's 678, copied, and six
written for the verdicts the mode was missing, each reaching the reference's
refusal: `OP_LSHIFTNUM` and `OP_RSHIFTNUM` by 2^31 (`shift count exceeds
INT_MAX.`, #383), a 9-byte `OP_LEFT` length read in two's complement
(`OP_LEFT length (-2) must be in range [0, 3]`) and an `OP_NUM2BIN` size of
2^31 (`OP_NUM2BIN size exceeds the node int32 push limit.`, #382), and
`1 <536,870,888> OP_LSHIFTNUM` and a 67,108,863-byte operand read by
`OP_1ADD` (`Invalid string length`, #331). Bit 3 of byte 0 selects a budget
of 128 MiB instead of 1 MiB: under 1 MiB the two #331 inputs are the budget's
declines (`Script element allocation has exceeded 1048576 bytes`), never the
read figure's verdict; 128 MiB holds one operand past the figure (V8's
`BigInt` cap, 2^30 bits, stays a decline here). Every copied seed has bit 3
clear. Measured on an 8 MiB squaring chain under the 128 MiB budget
(`0x7fffffff` and 21 `OP_DUP OP_MUL`), a build without a sanitizer peaks at a
resident set of 133 MB and `cargo fuzz`'s default AddressSanitizer build at
2,247 MB, where libFuzzer stops it as `out-of-memory (used: 2067Mb; limit:
2048Mb)` (3,394 MB with the limit off): the resident set is the sanitizer's
shadow and quarantine, not the interpreter's, and an `oom` artifact of that
accounting would hide a real one. So the nightly builds and runs this one
target with `-s none` (a matrix `sanitizer`, every other target keeping
AddressSanitizer): its subject is the interpreter's budget arithmetic and
refusals, panics and aborts libFuzzer catches without a sanitizer. A raised
`-rss_limit_mb` would mask the next real excess as well.

The nightly's fuzz matrix runs the new target (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`),
and `tests/arch_fuzz_targets_dispatched.rs` pins the matrix to
`fuzz/Cargo.toml`'s `[[bin]]`s both ways, every target to a seed corpus, and
this target's `sanitizer: none` with the build and run commands' `-s`.
On the tip, 90 seconds each from the seed corpus: `fuzz_script_spend` 1,398
executions, `fuzz_script_spend_default` 4,014, no crash. No public change.

### Fixed: discovery wire answers receive the reference's result validation (#495)

Both discovery calls now apply the shared `result_values` rows after their
typed wire read, in the reference's order. The deciding sites are
`ts-stack@edf6e03 WalletWireTransceiver.ts:1796-1800,1842-1846`;
`WalletResultValidation.ts:2288-2292` dispatches to `:1844-1916`, with
certificate validation at `:1477-1536`, page checks at `:1919-1938`, and
attribute matching at `:1577-1755`. This completes the two sites outside
#487's nine. The calls and discovery reader live in `wire/discovery.rs` to
keep `transceiver.rs` below its line ceiling. The shared implementation
validates metadata without a JSON round trip of byte fields or another
BEEF parse; it returns the original typed answer. The wire bytes, public
types, and all four `u32` totals are unchanged (the keeper's #467 ruling).

For the toolbox's and the CLI's verdict tables, every new refusal below is
an uncoded `Error::WalletError`. Let `C` be the discovery call name and `i`
the certificate index. The table gives the exact new words; the old verdict
is for a frame whose other rows pass.

| Row / discovery answer | Old verdict | New verdict / words |
|---|---|---|
| R03, either call: aggregate object graph exceeds the shared snapshot budget | Accepted | `Invalid C result object graph: expected a bounded result` |
| R74, either call: empty signature or DER scalar outside 1..n−1 | Accepted | `Invalid C result certificates[i]: expected a canonical signed wallet certificate` |
| R76, identity call: certificate subject differs from the requested identity key | Accepted | `Invalid discoverByIdentityKey result certificates[i].subject: expected the requested identity key` |
| R79, either call: certifier name outside 1–100 UTF-8 bytes | Accepted | `Invalid C result certificates[i].certifierInfo.name: expected 1–100 UTF-8 bytes` |
| R79, either call: icon URL outside 1–500 UTF-8 bytes, or not absolute HTTP(S) | Accepted | `Invalid C result certificates[i].certifierInfo.iconUrl: expected 1–500 UTF-8 bytes` or `Invalid C result certificates[i].certifierInfo.iconUrl: expected an absolute HTTP(S) URL` |
| R79, either call: certifier description outside 5–50 UTF-8 bytes | Accepted | `Invalid C result certificates[i].certifierInfo.description: expected 5–50 UTF-8 bytes` |
| R80, either call: empty publicly revealed keyring value | Accepted | `Invalid C result certificates[i].publiclyRevealedKeyring.name: expected 1+ UTF-8 bytes` (`name` is the actual field key) |
| R81, attributes call: `any` fails the reference's public-text search | Accepted | `Invalid discoverByAttributes result certificates[i].decryptedFields: expected a match for the requested any attribute` |
| R82, attributes call: named attribute absent or mismatched; no usable requested attribute | Accepted | `Invalid discoverByAttributes result certificates[i].decryptedFields.name: expected the requested public attribute` (`name` is the requested key), or `Invalid discoverByAttributes result certificates[i].decryptedFields: expected a usable requested attribute` |

Certificate identifier/key/outpoint forms, safe map keys and string values,
certificate size, trust 1–10, and page/count bounds already have typed or
wire-reader checks. Optional certificate `keyring` and `verifier` are absent
from discovery frames. List-only certifier/type filters do not apply to
these calls. Attribute search uses the same shared predicate as HTTP:
`any` excludes `profilePhoto`/`icon`, uses fuzzy matching for two characters
and English token/phrase/negative-term matching otherwise; named searches
ignore blank values, normalize `userName` for exact matching, and match
other fields' literal tokens in order within a line.

### Fixed: streaming BEEF heap pin keeps exact equality under CI's harness (#372)

The streaming reader's heap pin checks one chunk and one element at 1,000,
10,000 and 100,000 links with exact equality across depths. The chain sources
and headers stay outside the measured region; the observed stream-alone
peak is 17,004 bytes at every depth. No tolerance is added: one sized to the warning would have
to grow with the number of tests that time out together. The
32 KiB ceiling, verifier index's per-element bounds and NL-3 meaning stay.

The pin is judged under `--test-threads=1`, using CI's command,
`cargo test --test memory_profiling --all-features -- --test-threads=1`
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml:236`, with `--verbose` in CI). Libtest 1.95.0's
single-threaded path waits on `rx.recv()` and never warns
([`library/test/src/lib.rs:415-436`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.95.0/library/test/src/lib.rs#L415-L436)).
Only the concurrent path issues the 60-second timeout warning
([`:437-460`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.95.0/library/test/src/lib.rs#L437-L460)).
A default-harness run that lets several tests reach that warning is outside
the pin's condition, even though their bodies wait on `serial()`.

Dhat counts harness allocations too. `get_timed_out_tests` builds a
`Vec<TestDesc>` containing every test whose timer has expired when the
harness wakes
([`library/test/src/lib.rs:390-406`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.95.0/library/test/src/lib.rs#L390-L406));
`PrettyFormatter::write_timeout` formats one message `String` per test
([`formatters/pretty.rs:258-264`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.95.0/library/test/src/formatters/pretty.rs#L258-L264)).
A one-test warning at an element boundary caused the observed 56-byte delta
before setup moved out of the profile (17,152 versus 17,096 bytes).
The first attempt's 676-byte allowance fitted one timed-out test; the vector
grows with the batch, so no fixed allowance covers the whole diagnostic. On this branch
11 other tests can wait on `serial()` while the pin runs (12 with #493).
No reader or wire code changes.

On an archived `a962ef49`, the first attempt, which carried a 676-byte
allowance, a control with ten extra sleeping tests holds the boundary after dropping the first element at 100,000 links until 61 seconds
from the test's start. The allowance and exact-equality variants both fail
under the default harness: stream-alone peaks of 18,596 and 29,771 bytes,
respectively, versus 17,004 bytes at the smaller depths. These runs are
outside the pin's condition, not REDs to make green.
The single-test control with the same delay and `--test-threads=1` passes at
17,004 bytes at every depth, without a timeout warning.
Five unforced runs of the pin with `--test-threads=1` also pass at 17,004
bytes at all three depths.

### Fixed: refuse oversized wallet wire requests before transmission (#496)

`WalletWireTransceiver` now refuses a complete request frame above 256 MiB
(268,435,456 bytes) after building the frame and before calling the transport,
including before allocating its future. The named request bound sits beside
the existing response cap. The refusal is
`Error::WalletError("Wallet Wire request exceeds the maximum permitted size")`,
without an SDK code, as for the client-side refusals in #473 and #487. A frame
exactly at the cap is sent; argument validation, originator normalization,
serialization and all behavior at or below the cap are unchanged.

The deciding reference is `ts-stack@edf6e03`:
`WalletWire.ts:9` defines `MAX_WALLET_WIRE_FRAME_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024`;
`WalletWireTransceiver.ts:95-104` normalizes the originator and builds the frame,
`:104-107` throws `Error('Wallet Wire request exceeds the maximum permitted size')`,
then `:108-133` sends and bounds the response. The call's argument validation
already ran (`:938` for encrypt, before its parameter writer). This follows
the owner's ruling (c) of 2026-10-26: the reference's own behavior.

The toolbox's and CLI's tables change as follows:

| Consumer | Request | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Toolbox error table | Complete frame above 268,435,456 bytes | Sent to the transport; no client frame-size refusal | `WalletError`, no SDK code: `Wallet Wire request exceeds the maximum permitted size` |
| CLI operator-visible table | Complete frame above 268,435,456 bytes | Sent to the transport; any later transport or wallet outcome | Local failure before sending: `wallet error: Wallet Wire request exceeds the maximum permitted size` |
| Both | Complete frame at or below 268,435,456 bytes | Sent | Sent, with unchanged bytes and response handling |

`tests/wallet_wire_request_frame_cap_496.rs` pins two boundaries through a
counting stub wallet: cap + 1 refuses with zero transport and wallet calls;
cap sends once, reaches the wallet once and returns its answer. On the base,
the first sent and reached the wallet; the second already passed. The #487
recorder's `--request-frame-cap-496` mode writes both frame recipes and hashes
under Node 22.18.0; two runs are byte-identical. The at-cap bytes are captured
from the reference's compact transport. Its transceiver cannot emit an
oversized frame, so that candidate is built by the SDK writer from the captured
header and trailer, and the reference processor supplies the same uncoded
refusal with zero wallet calls. No frame is handwritten.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#496)

The TypeScript processor also rejects oversized requests before decoding or
wallet dispatch (`WalletWireProcessor.ts:248-269`), with the same uncoded
words on both legacy and compact inputs. This change is the transceiver's
guard only; this crate's processor retains its existing behavior without a
whole-request cap. Go at `2ca481c` has no corresponding frame cap:
`wallet/serializer/frame.go:19-36` writes the full request and
`wallet/substrates/wallet_wire_transceiver.go:23-35` immediately transmits it.
The request bound follows TypeScript; Go's behavior differs above it.
The reference's processor does not answer the recorded at-cap frame end to end:
under Node 22.18.0 `Array.from` of the 268,435,414-byte plaintext
(`WalletWireProcessor.ts:1427`) fails on V8's array limit with code 1
`Invalid array length` and no wallet call, so the at-cap test's answer comes from
the reference's transceiver over a stub transport and this crate's processor
(the cold review's measurement). The processor's own cap is bsv-rs#505.

### Fixed: local KVStore parser words inside Original error (#489)

Local authentication now uses the reference's parser messages for inputs
that the reference also refuses with those messages, inside the
`Invalid value found. Relinquish the corrupted output from the {context}
basket before using this key again. Original error: {message}` wrapper.
Previously, a malformed locking key or token exposed this crate's native
hex, public-key or script-parser diagnostic. The local parser catches select
the reference text by error variant, input shape and the reference's point
acceptance rules; if the reference accepts the key, the native parser error
is retained. They do not compare diagnostic strings or change acceptance
or the primitives' own errors. Wallet-supplied
errors still follow #477's extraction rule, including an injected
`InvalidPublicKey` error. No public shape changes; update matches on the
wrapped parser suffixes below. Local parser failures use `KvStoreLocalError`,
including authentication during remove, where there is no lookup wrapper.

The deciding reference is `ts-stack@edf6e03`, under Node 22.18.0:
`LocalKVStore.ts:239-246` derives and parses the locking key, `:278-282`
calls `decodeCanonicalPushDrop`, and `:340-345` wraps `error.message`.
`PublicKey.ts:49-51` delegates to `Point.fromString` (`Point.ts:345-347`);
`utils.ts:126-128` and `hex.ts:6-15` reject non-hex text. `Point.ts:303-325`
distinguishes an unknown length/prefix from a point off the curve
(`:280-283,365-372`); hybrid `06`/`07` keys with the wrong Y parity throw
`Point string value is wrong length` before the curve check (`:309-317`).
`PushDropValidation.ts:54-74` calls
`PushDrop.decode` at `:59`: its default lock-before path reads the initial
chunk's key at `PushDrop.ts:73-77`, then the fields at `:96-115`, before
the canonical decoder checks field count and envelope. These are the actual
lines at the pin: the key parse is `LocalKVStore.ts:246`, not `:248`, the
canonical decode is `:278-282`, and the authentication catch is `:340-345`.
Go at `2ca481c`, `kvstore/local_kv_store.go:66-111`, uses operation wrappers
and has no equivalent `Original error:` contract.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#489)

This crate's key parsing is stricter than the reference's: no odd-length
padding, no hybrid keys, no x reduced mod p. At `ts-stack@edf6e03`,
`hex.ts:28-30` pads odd hex, `Point.ts:303-325` accepts on-curve hybrid keys
with matching parity, and `Point.ts:365-384` reduces x modulo p. Thus
`PublicKey.fromString` (`PublicKey.ts:49-51`, `Point.ts:345-347`) accepts the
key classes the table below samples (odd-length keys such as `3`+Gx and
`4`+Gx+Gy, hybrid keys with the matching parity, and any x reduced mod p in
compressed, uncompressed or hybrid form) that `PublicKey::from_hex` refuses here. A token with either
accepted noncanonical key push decodes there, then fails the canonical
envelope check (`LocalKVStore.ts:278-282`, `PushDropValidation.ts:73-74`).
Here it fails key parsing earlier. The words here are the parser's own,
including its error-category prefix, never a reference refusal invented
for an accepted input. Gx/Gy below are the secp256k1 generator coordinates;
p is the field prime. Key acceptance is unchanged by this fold.

The reference's local-store site decodes lock-before only
(`LocalKVStore.ts:278-282`, `PushDropValidation.ts:59`, `PushDrop.ts:74-75`).
This crate's general decoder also tries lock-after and reaches a later
field-count or canonical-envelope check. The two existing differences are
pinned below, including both SDKs' full wrapped messages. Restricting this
site to lock-before is a separate behavior decision.

| Input | Recorded reference verdict | This crate after `Original error:` | Pin in `kvstore_local_parser_words_489.rs` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2` + Gx | Key accepted; later wallet-key mismatch | `invalid hex string: Odd number of digits` | `reference_accepts_odd_valid_key_but_local_keeps_native_words_489` |
| `06` + Gx + Gy | Key accepted; later wallet-key mismatch | `invalid public key: Invalid public key encoding: elliptic curve point encoding error` | `reference_accepts_hybrid_key_but_local_keeps_native_words_489` |
| `6` + Gx + Gy | Key accepted; later wallet-key mismatch | `invalid hex string: Odd number of digits` | `reference_accepts_odd_hybrid_key_but_local_keeps_native_words_489` |
| `02` + (p+1) | Key accepted; later wallet-key mismatch | `invalid public key: Point not on curve` | `reference_accepts_reduced_x_key_but_local_keeps_native_words_489` |
| Token key `06` + Gx + Gy | Decodes; `PushDrop token must use the canonical PushDrop envelope` | `invalid public key: Invalid public key encoding: elliptic curve point encoding error` | `reference_decodes_hybrid_token_but_local_keeps_native_words_489` |
| Token key `02` + (p+1) | Decodes; `PushDrop token must use the canonical PushDrop envelope` | `invalid public key: Point not on curve` | `reference_decodes_reduced_x_token_but_local_keeps_native_words_489` |
| `51 75 <G> ac` | `script.chunks[0].data must have value` | `Unexpected PushDrop token field count` | `lock_after_one_field_reaches_local_field_count_not_reference_decode_489` |
| `51 52 6d <G> ac` | `script.chunks[0].data must have value` | `PushDrop token must use the canonical PushDrop envelope` | `lock_after_two_fields_reaches_local_envelope_not_reference_decode_489` |

The reference's words in the two lock-after rows come from its lock-before
parse of the first chunk, so they vary with it: a first chunk that is a data
push but no key (`00 75 <G> ac`) gets `Unknown point format` there; here the
field count or the envelope check speaks, as in the rows.

The recorder now writes 52 cases (26 inputs, each for get and set), including
an explicit `parser_accepted` verdict for these eight inputs. Two Node
22.18.0 runs are byte-identical; all earlier fields and the 36 original
cases are unchanged. With the new test file and recorded vector overlaid
on an archived `9bcbe433`, the six accepted-key/token tests are RED because
the tip incorrectly reports `Invalid point`; the two lock-after pins and
the original five tests are already green. All 13 tests pass after the
fold. The RED scratch copy uses its own target directory and is removed.

### Fixed: local removal stops after two rounds (#483)

`LocalKVStore::remove` counts completed page spends and refuses a third spend,
even when every reported total shrinks. Before this change the loop had no
bound: a wallet that kept answering fresh, authenticated outputs under a total
that did not shrink kept the removal spending forever, page after page, as the
reference's `LocalKVStore.ts:574-590` still does. The keeper's policy (02:1xZ on #483)
is two rounds: the reference keeps one current token per key, and a second
round covers a token written during the first. One token per page under a
larger total is an inconsistent wallet answer; ten thousand spends for one
key is the exposure this bound refuses. Removal costs at most three listings
and two spends for any wallet. A complete page within the cap, or an empty
page with total zero, still completes normally.

The cap is checked first after #479's unchanged empty-page check, before any
further authentication or spend. The shrinking rule remains beneath it: the
second listing's total must fall below the first's. A plateau or rise is
refused there. Both guards return `Error::KvStoreLocalError`, displayed without
a category prefix, with the operation's completed rounds, totals and key:

| Guard | Refusal words (example) |
| --- | --- |
| Two-round cap, third listing | `Wallet returned an inconsistent KVStore output list: after 2 removal rounds, first totalOutputs was 7, previous totalOutputs was 6 and current totalOutputs is 5 for key alpha` |
| Shrinking guard, second listing | `Wallet returned an inconsistent KVStore output list: after 1 removal round, previous totalOutputs was 7 and current totalOutputs is 7 for key alpha` |

Earlier spends remain spent; an error never reports their txids as complete
removal. A nonempty third listing cannot spend even if its page equals its
total. A third listing with total zero completes without another spend.

| Policy | Bound and reason | Reference | Change rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_LOCAL_REMOVE_ROUNDS`: two completed page spends; shrinking totals beneath the cap | At most three listings and two spends for any wallet. One current token per key plus one written during the first round; a wallet listing one token at a time under a larger total must not expose that key to 10,000 spends. The second listing must shrink below the first. | `ts-stack@edf6e03` `LocalKVStore.ts:574-590` has no round bound. `set` spends the previous tokens and writes one (`:373-382,455,496,515-528`). | The constant is the sole production round-policy number; change it by a measurement, never silently. |

`tests/kvstore_local_rounds_483.rs` uses writer-built signed tokens in fresh
transactions on every page. On an archived `33fd45b5` with this test file
overlaid, the 7, 6, 5, ... witness makes seven listings and seven spends instead
of stopping at three and two. Second-listing plateau (7, 7) and rise (7, 8)
witnesses also fail there: that fold only compared totals from the third
listing. The 7, 6, 6 witness still stops on the third listing, now by the cap
rather than the shrinking guard; its exact words assert that distinction.
All eight tests pass with both guards, including one-round removal, two-round
removal for a token written during the first, third-listing zero-total
completion, and #479 empty-page precedence. The four tests in
`kvstore_local_empty_page_479.rs` pass on both; the #454 recorded vectors are
unchanged.

Migration: handle the refusal in the existing local-store error variant;
earlier spends do not establish complete removal. Consistent one- and
two-round wallet requests and their bytes are unchanged; no public API is added.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#483)

At `ts-stack@edf6e03`, `LocalKVStore.ts:574-590` repeats the same listing
request, authenticates and spends one page per round (`:585`), and exits only
when the page length equals the reported total (`:587`). Distinct outputs
bypass its consumed-output check. Its `set` gathers the previous token inputs
at `:373-382,455,496` and spends them while writing one replacement at
`:515-528`. By the keeper's word (02:1xZ on #483), this crate caps removal at
two rounds, with the shrinking guard beneath it, for at most three listings
and two spends for any wallet. One current token plus a token written during
the first round is the reason; an inconsistent wallet cannot demand ten
thousand spends for a key. The reference has no bound at `:574-590` and no
such typed, counted refusal. This is a deliberate policy divergence, changed
only by a measurement and never silently.

Census (#375; current reading, historical account above retained):
