### Fixed: local KVStore original-error messages omit family prefixes (#477)

The shared `original_error_message` helper now reads `WalletFault.message`
and the payloads of `BeefError` and `TransactionError` at every local wrapper.
Previously those variants inserted Rust's category prefix after `Original
error:`. `WalletError`, `KvStoreError` and `KvStoreLocalError` keep their entire
strings, including any prefix that is part of the payload. Other variants keep
their own Display diagnostics. The outer variant remains `KvStoreLocalError`;
no public API or standalone error Display changes.

The reference is `ts-stack@edf6e03`: the two lookup catches at
`LocalKVStore.ts:315-321,340-345`, removal at `:427-430` and replacement at
`:547-550` all read `error.message`. `WalletError.ts:3-16` calls
`super(message)` without a category. `Beef.ts:1251-1254,1296-1308` and
`Transaction.ts:302-311` throw ordinary `Error`s. At this pin, the finding's
`:227` is lock cleanup; the lookup wrappers are the lines cited above.

Rows for the toolbox's error table; these are the exact words after
`Original error:` (`\n` denotes the actual newline in the wallet message):

| Variant | Old words | New words |
|---|---|---|
| `WalletFault` (every family) | `wallet error: backend: café\nretry` | `backend: café\nretry` |
| `BeefError` | `BEEF error: invalid BEEF at byte 0: BadVersion { word: 0 }` | `invalid BEEF at byte 0: BadVersion { word: 0 }` |
| `TransactionError` | `transaction error: Not an Atomic BEEF format` | `Not an Atomic BEEF format` |
| `WalletError` | `wallet error: preserve this payload` | Unchanged |
| `KvStoreError` | `kvstore error: preserve this payload` | Unchanged |
| `KvStoreLocalError` | `local: preserve this payload` | Unchanged |
| Every other enabled variant | Its own Display text | Unchanged |

The `wallet error:` and `kvstore error:` texts in the `WalletError` and
`KvStoreError` rows are the test payloads themselves, not prefixes: a
`WalletError(String)` and a `KvStoreError(String)` carry their whole payload
unchanged. `WalletBusy`, `WalletTransport` and `TransportFault` keep their
Display (`wallet busy: …` and the transport texts) by choice: the reference
has no error of those kinds to take a message from.

Rows for the CLI's operator-visible table (the same suffix applies to the
lookup wrapper and the count/key action wrapper):

| Failure | Old suffix | New suffix |
|---|---|---|
| Wallet storage/service/transport/internal fault | `wallet error: backend: café\nretry` | `backend: café\nretry` |
| BEEF with version zero | `BEEF error: invalid BEEF at byte 0: BadVersion { word: 0 }` | `invalid BEEF at byte 0: BadVersion { word: 0 }` |
| Non-atomic BEEF where an action requires Atomic BEEF | `transaction error: Not an Atomic BEEF format` | `Not an Atomic BEEF format` |

`tests/kvstore_local_original_error_477.rs` has nine tests. Five fail on base
`5981e285a6594ff1e3f7b67b21137c2ce3bc08e5` because the whole wrapped string
contains the extra category: one per changed variant plus two actual corrupt
response cases. The three existing payload variants and the other-variant
Display control pass there. All nine pass with the helper. The injected cases
exercise both lookup catches and both action wrappers; all four fault families
are tested. The #326 recorder's `--kvstore-local-454` mode adds 60 injected
cases and six malformed-response cases to `kvstore_local_454.json`, produced
twice byte-identically under Node 22.18.0. The four existing action recordings
are unchanged. Migration: update matches on these three wrapped suffixes only.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#477)

The original-error extraction now follows the reference. The parsers' existing
diagnostic differences remain: for version-zero BEEF the reference says
`Serialized BEEF must start with 4022206465 or 4022206466 but starts with 0`,
where this crate says `invalid BEEF at byte 0: BadVersion { word: 0 }`; for
non-atomic action BEEF the reference says `beef must conform to BRC-95 and must
contain the subject txid.`, where this crate says `Not an Atomic BEEF format`.
These are recorded divergences, not claimed whole-message parity for malformed
BEEF. The tests compare both references' wrappers exactly when their input
messages agree and separately pin the Rust parsers' unchanged words.
Go at `2ca481c`, `kvstore/local_kv_store.go:70-111,347-363,498-516`, wraps errors
with operation names and has no equivalent `Original error:` contract; the
TypeScript reference decides this change.

### Fixed: wallet wire numeric and pre-entry collection bounds (#473)

The wire readers now make the reference's checks before reading entries or
allocating their collections. The reference is the unmodified `ts-stack@edf6e03`
under Node v22.18.0. `tests/wallet_wire_bounds_473.rs` replays the #338 recorder's
`--bounds-473` mode (`tests/support/wire_bounds_473.mjs`): 73 cases, two runs
byte-identical, 39 regression tests. Each test is RED on base
`f9c99065c3ff2bd7395cdfb6cd5238156fd48bab` and GREEN with the bounds.

`getHeight` reads `readVarIntNumStrict(false)`, checks trailing bytes, then
requires 1 through 4294967295 (`WalletWireTransceiver.ts:1882-1888`). Nine `ff`
bytes are **not** absence here: the unsigned read refuses them. The signed
reader's `-1` sentinel is only available when `signed` is true
(`primitives/readVarIntNumStrict.ts:15-36`, especially `:33-35`). The result
validator's `getHeight` row says
`rangedInteger(result.height, call, 'height', 1, 0xffffffff)`
(`WalletResultValidation.ts:2293-2294`); its expectation is
`an integer from 1 to 4294967295` (`:946-958`). The transceiver's own refusal,
which comes first on the client, is `Wallet returned an invalid height`.

The three formerly unbounded unsigned satoshi reads are all **result-side**:

| Rust read | Reference strict read and range | Result validator |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WireReader::read_wallet_action_input`, `source_satoshis` | `WalletWireTransceiver.ts:480-485`, `listActions input sourceSatoshis`, 0 through 21e14 | `WalletResultValidation.ts:2010`, `uint(input.sourceSatoshis, ..., 21e14)` |
| `WireReader::read_wallet_action_output`, `satoshis` | `WalletWireTransceiver.ts:523-528`, `listActions output satoshis`, 0 through 21e14 | `WalletResultValidation.ts:2053`, `uint(output.satoshis, ..., 21e14)` |
| `WireReader::read_wallet_output`, `satoshis` | `WalletWireTransceiver.ts:670-675`, `listOutputs satoshis`, 0 through 21e14 | `WalletResultValidation.ts:2105`, `uint(output.satoshis, ..., 21e14)` |

The common domain is also explicit in `validationHelpers.ts:266-270`:
`!Number.isSafeInteger(v) || v < 0 || v > 21e14` throws
`WERR_INVALID_PARAMETER(name, 'a valid number of satoshis')`. That helper is
**request-side**, called by `validateCreateActionOutput` at `:635`, after
`WalletWireProcessor.ts:376` reads the amount strictly. It is not the function
invoked by the three result readers. Those use `#requireInteger`'s words
(`WalletWireTransceiver.ts:2018-2025`), and then the result validator's `uint`
(`WalletResultValidation.ts:935-943`). Precision is checked before the range.

V's common array bound is `an array of at most 100000 items` (`:105-114`),
its object bound `an object with at most 100000 properties` (`:90-91`). R's
common array bound is `at most 100000 entries` (`:971-975`), used by
`stringArray` (`:978-987`) and the result paths above. Snapshotting separately
limits the result object graph to 1000000 nodes/properties and an array to
1000000 entries (`R:215-219,688-742,772-814`); these are post-decode object
checks, not additional wire collection lengths. Certificate binary fields are
already bounded at their own count (`auth/certificates/Certificate.ts:356-387`;
`wire/mod.rs::read_certificate_fields`), not a second request-record encoding.

There is no uncapped logical entry array in these two reference files: each is
covered above or by the page/result validators. Byte sequences are not subject
to the 100000-entry collection cap: transaction/BEEF, scripts, error text,
linkage/proof, encrypted/plain data, signatures/HMACs, certificate payloads,
UTF-8 strings and keys keep their existing byte/domain checks. In particular a
page's *total* remains a u32 total, not capped to its page length. Rust's public
standalone `read_string_array`, `read_string_map`, `read_optional_string_map`
retain their generic behavior; no arbitrary collection cap was added to them.
Unimplemented request handlers remain unimplemented, and their missing parsing
is not claimed fixed by this change.

within the requested limit retain their readings. Complete satoshi values at
2100000000000000, heights 1 and 4294967295, and ten-entry pages are recorded
successes. Truncated collections now use the reference's availability words.

before the entry and allocation; counted records retain u64 until the maximum
and remaining bytes have been checked, including on wasm32; no dependency or public signature changes.

All 71 tests were RED on a scratch copy of `455fe78092952a22e4f386ac22642987dbf8120a`
with an independent Cargo target. The extended #408 Node 22.18.0 recorder
preserves its 387 existing cases byte for byte and adds 626 cases (126 accepted,
500 refused), for 1,013 total. The cold-review fold adds seven R03 cases and
disambiguates thirteen duplicate case names; every earlier body, request and
reference verdict remains byte-identical. It generates every new case
from the unmodified edf6e03 SDK built outside the worktree. Large boundary
cases use expansion recipes. A repeated recording is compared byte for byte.
HTTP tests bind only wiremock ephemeral ports, including HTTP/2 for the
oversized Content-Length header; no default wallet endpoint is contacted. The
existing `fixtures_replay` recorder also refreshes seven HTTP golden files:
only `client_result` changes (empty actions, unbound BEEF, false verdicts and
network words); every request, raw response and non-HTTP fixture is unchanged.
The #339 review test now matches the reference in 39 of 41 cases, removing
its transaction-binding exception; its successful retry mock supplies both
the signed transaction and its computed txid.

The cold-review regressions in `wallet_http_json_linear_432` compare the three
4 MiB bodies at depths 2,000, 4,000 and 8,000 on success and error paths. The
median time ratio is bounded against the smallest body's byte-size ratio,
without an absolute time limit. They also preserve the final duplicate field
value on the raw fallback and ignore unrelated deep/nonfinite extensions
inside code-5 result records. R03's seven added recorder cases cover both
height spellings, the two error envelopes and the lone-surrogate residue.

Migration: callers that branched on `valid: false` or `authenticated: false`
now handle an `Err`.
Wrapped heights, unrelated BEEF and mismatched request or filter facts are
also refused in the reference's words; public field types stay unchanged.

The `http` feature adds optional `regex` and enables the existing optional
`unicode-normalization`: the reference's identity search uses `\p{Dash}`,
`\p{Pattern_Syntax}`, `\p{Quotation_Mark}`, `\p{Terminal_Punctuation}` and
`\p{Mn}` plus NFD (`WalletResultValidation.ts:1577-1582,1617-1619`), which the
serde model cannot express. `regex`, `regex-automata` and `regex-syntax` are
MIT OR Apache-2.0; `aho-corasick` is Unlicense OR MIT. The dependency tree grows
by the regex family (`regex`, `regex-automata`, `regex-syntax`, `aho-corasick`);
the exact line count depends on the lockfile's resolution. The combined wasm32 slice
(`auth,wallet,transaction,overlay,socketio,wasm`, without native-only `http`)
builds. `regex-syntax` uses Unicode 16.0, as Node 22.18.0's ICU 77.1 does;
`unicode-normalization` 0.1.26 uses Unicode 18.0. This table-version difference
can move identity-search results when tables change. Six compiled expressions
are cached in `LazyLock`s, available below the Rust 1.88 minimum.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#432)

The 88-row inventory has 85 fully Done rows and three stated residue rows,
with no Pending work hidden. R02's executable JavaScript values, descriptors,
prototypes, sparse arrays, shared/detached typed arrays and aliasing are not
HTTP JSON values. R03 checks the expressible budgets; its aggregate-byte cap
is dominated by the bounded 256 MiB JSON body. The cold-review fold indexes
containers on a heap stack in one scan and walks their links for budgets;
it never reparses a descendant through each ancestor and keeps no Value per
ordinary byte. Its fallback normalizes raw tokens and historical byte objects,
so an unrelated `1e400` or depth-129 array no longer defeats an integral `1.0`
height. Node 22.18.0 at edf6e03 accepts both (height 1), reads `1e400` as Infinity
and has no JSON depth bound; serde's typed 128-level guard stays enabled here.
Code-5 error envelopes and their nested result records select known members
from the raw body, likewise ignoring unrelated extras. Lone UTF-16 surrogates
are the true R03 residue:
`{"version":"123456\ud800"}` is accepted there, refused here with
`Invalid getVersion result version: expected a string`.
R47 checks 0 through 2^53-1 at the JSON validator's bound and keeps the public
`u32` list totals: on the keeper's word (03:1xZ, #467 (a)) `u32` is the width
of BRC-100 (`wallet/0100.md:274`), the reference's typedef (`@maximum
4294967295`), its wire reader and processor, and Go; the JSON validator's
2^53-1 at `WalletResultValidation.ts:1926` is one layer against four, a stated
residue filed upstream as ts-stack #1449. Five wide-total cases still assert
serde's range refusal above 2^32-1.
The native byte form of a signable reference does not preserve a base64
padding-bit spelling, as described above.

Go's `~/bsv/go-sdk/wallet/substrates/http_wallet_json.go` at local `2ca481c`
uses `api` (`:37-75`) to read the body and method-specific `json.Unmarshal`
(`:79-400`) to decode it. It has no `validateWalletResult` equivalent, no
request/filter/BEEF binding or global graph/byte/unsafe-key checks. Its typed
integers and keys can reject shapes in Go's words but do not provide these
reference checks or this refusal order. Existing #137 error-class mapping and
transport-fault policies remain port extensions.

### Fixed: local removal refuses an empty page under a positive total (#479)

`LocalKVStore::remove` now ends on the first empty page whose `totalOutputs` is
positive. Previously it repeated the same request forever. The refusal is
`Error::KvStoreLocalError`, with the local store's own words, displayed without
a category prefix: `Wallet returned an inconsistent KVStore output list:
totalOutputs is 7, but page at offset 0 is empty for key alpha` for the reported
witness. The total and key come from that operation. Each removal request omits
the offset (zero), even after a preceding page has been spent; the diagnostic
reports that request offset, not the number already consumed. A later empty
page returns an error even if earlier pages were spent, never a partial txid
list as a successful complete removal. Earlier spends are not rolled back.

`tests/kvstore_local_empty_page_479.rs` bounds each removal with a one-second
timeout and a yielding stub wallet. The initial-empty and post-spend-empty
tests time out on base `cc17b9cbb86923ac31df869d002eca43af414f51`; the consistent
two-page and zero-total controls pass there. All four pass with the guard.
Consistent wallet requests and the recorded #454 vectors remain unchanged.

Migration: no new variant or public shape; callers must handle this new
`KvStoreLocalError` refusal instead of waiting indefinitely or assuming a
partial removal completed. Its message is local-store text, not reference text.

without reading a total or paging in a loop; it is unchanged too.

### Fixed: the wire originator drops one leading byte-order mark (#471)

The processor now removes one leading U+FEFF (`ef bb bf`) after the strict
UTF-8 check and before checking for an empty originator or validating its
hostname. A BOM-only header reaches the wallet as `None`, as an empty header
does (#329), instead of receiving code 6. This follows the reference's own
behavior under the owner's ruling (c) of 2026-10-26; no refusal words change.

At `ts-stack@edf6e03`, `packages/sdk/src/primitives/utils.ts:224-228`
implements `toUTF8Strict` with `new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true })`.
Its default `ignoreBOM: false` removes exactly one leading BOM, as specified
by the [WHATWG serialization rule](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-td-serialize)
and witnessed under Node v22.18.0. `WalletWireProcessor.ts:286-294` decodes
before the empty-string check and `validateOriginator` call. A second or
nonleading BOM survives decoding; the validator then trims edge U+FEFF
characters (`wallet/validationHelpers.ts:1003-1006`). Consequently all
three hostname examples below reach the wallet as `a.b` on both versions.

Rows for the toolbox's behavior table (`BOM` means U+FEFF):

| Wire originator | Old decoding and result | New decoding and reference result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BOM` | BOM kept; code 6, `The originator parameter must be at least 1 length.` | Empty; code 0, wallet originator `None` (reference `''`) |
| `BOM` + `a.b` | BOM kept; validation trims it; code 0, `a.b` | `a.b`; code 0, `a.b` |
| `BOM` + `BOM` + `a.b` | Both BOMs kept; validation trims them; code 0, `a.b` | Second BOM kept; validation trims it; code 0, `a.b` |
| `a.b` + `BOM` | Trailing BOM kept; validation trims it; code 0, `a.b` | Trailing BOM kept; validation trims it; code 0, `a.b` |

Rows for the CLI's operator-visible table:

| Wire originator | Old code and words or wallet value | New code and words or wallet value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BOM` | 6, `The originator parameter must be at least 1 length.` | 0, absent originator (`None`) |
| `BOM` + `a.b` | 0, `a.b` (BOM kept until validation) | 0, `a.b` (leading BOM removed before validation) |
| `BOM` + `BOM` + `a.b` | 0, `a.b` (both BOMs kept until validation) | 0, `a.b` (second BOM kept until validation) |
| `a.b` + `BOM` | 0, `a.b` (trailing BOM kept until validation) | 0, `a.b` (trailing BOM kept until validation) |

`tests/support/wire_originator_338.mjs`, invoked through the #406 recorder,
writes all four processor cases to `tests/vectors/wallet_wire/originator_338.json`,
including their decoded strings, response frames, codes, refusal messages
(`null` for these four successes) and wallet observations. Two runs are
byte-identical; all seventeen prior processor cases, nine transceiver cases,
the length probes and the linkage recording are unchanged.
`tests/wallet_wire_originator_bom_471.rs` tests each case separately. On a
scratch copy of base `ad6e350a7407409860e9df481fb8453eab001bfe`, BOM-only is
RED on the old code-6 refusal; the three hostname cases are passing controls
because their observable behavior already matches the reference. All four
are GREEN with the reader change. Four REDs would misstate the reference.

Go at `2ca481c` reads the originator bytes with `ReadBytes` and converts them
directly with `string(originatorBytes)` (`wallet/serializer/frame.go:49-58`);
it does not strip a BOM. This crate follows the TypeScript decoder. The
TypeScript transceiver (`WalletWireTransceiver.ts:95-100`) validates the
caller's string and encodes the normalized result, without decoding it;
there is no outgoing TextDecoder BOM rule. Its validator already trims edge
BOMs and still refuses a BOM-only caller string. This change is reader-only.

### Changed: per-input verification work budget (#378, part 2)

`Transaction::verify_with_work_budget` and
`verify_with_chain_params_and_work_budget` add an optional work budget beside
the memory budget. Both stream verifiers add `with_work_budget`, beside the
existing `set_work_limit`. Each input uses the same `SpendParams::work_limit`
counter: reached opcodes and bytes hashed, reserved before execution.

A refused charge is `NotJudgedCause::WorkBudgetExceeded { input, budget,
work_done }`, carried by `Error::TransactionNotJudged`,
`SpendRefusal::NotJudged` and `Verdict::NotJudged`. Migration: callers
matching `set_work_limit` exhaustion through `SpendRefusal::Resource` must now
match `SpendRefusal::NotJudged` and its `NotJudgedCause::WorkBudgetExceeded`
cause. The diagnostic names the input once, the budget and already charged
work, never script failure. A spend inside the budget keeps its verdict; the
memory-budget classes and checks are unchanged. The work budget does not
interrupt a running arithmetic opcode or impose an elapsed-time bound.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#378, part 2)

The reference's `Transaction.verify` has no work bound. Existing crate entry
points and both new budget surfaces default to `None`, preserving that
behavior byte for byte. The budget is each service door's policy: the
toolbox's internalize and signer, the engine's script door and the tracker's
door set it at their re-pin, each brief naming its value beside the sibling's
memory rows. `tests/transaction_work_budget_378.rs` covers whole, sync and
async verification, exact and exhausted budgets, deferred inputs, resume and
unchanged verdicts; it also pins `NotJudgedCause` at 24 bytes and `Error` at
56 on 64-bit targets, with the cause's input index a `u32` as in the streaming

### Fixed: the wire header refusals use the reference's words (#458)

The processor's bad-UTF-8 originator refusal is now
`The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8`, replacing
`invalid originator UTF-8`. A truncated originator of at most 250 declared
bytes is now `ReaderUint8Array read exceeds available data`, replacing
`reader underflow: need N bytes, only M available`. Both still carry code 1.
These are the errors from `WalletWireProcessor.ts:292-293`,
`utils.ts:224-228` (`toUTF8Strict`, Node v22.18.0), and
`ReaderUint8Array.ts:38-59` at `ts-stack@edf6e03`; the processor frames them
at `WalletWireProcessor.ts:2379-2396`.

The latter sentence belongs to the reader, not only the originator.
`wire/reader.rs` now holds the basic `WireReader` methods and translates
short reads of bytes, `u8`, `i8`, little-endian `u16`/`u32`/`u64`, and
varints to `WalletError` with those words. Signed and optional varints use
the same path. For varint byte lengths, `wire_length` checks the reference's
`2^53 - 1` precision bound before the available bytes or platform width:
`2^53` through `u64::MAX` at an unsigned site is
`number too large to retain precision - use readVarIntBn`, code 1 in a
processor response. Optional lengths retain `u64::MAX` as absence; a signed
`-1` passed to a byte read has the reader's refusal. This applies to request
headers and parameters, response payloads, and error-frame message and stack
reads. The primitives `Reader`
retains its typed `ReaderUnderflow { needed, available }`; other errors
are unchanged. The processor stays at 929 lines.

Migration: replace `Error::ReaderUnderflow { .. }` matches on `WireReader` short reads with `Error::WalletError(message)` matching `ReaderUint8Array read exceeds available data`; the primitives `Reader` keeps `ReaderUnderflow`.

The checked `u8::try_from` in `wire/originator.rs` is retained with a comment:
its error arm cannot run because `validate_originator` has already capped
the normalized hostname at 250 bytes. There is no behavior change there.

Rows for the toolbox's operator-visible table:

|---|---|---|
| Bad-UTF-8 originator | 1, `invalid originator UTF-8` | 1, `The encoded data was not valid for encoding utf-8` |
| Truncated originator, declared length at most 250; any other short request read | 1, `reader underflow: need N bytes, only M available` | 1, `ReaderUint8Array read exceeds available data` |
| `listActions totalActions` or `listOutputs totalOutputs` is `2^53` | Local `WalletError`: `Invalid <field>: expected an integer from 0 to 4294967295, received 9007199254740992` | Local `WalletError`: `number too large to retain precision - use readVarIntBn` |
| This crate writes a string-array entry `""` | Nine `0xFF`, refused by the earlier fold's reader | `00`, read back as `""` |
| Go string-array entry encoded as nine `0xFF` | Read as `""` before #458 | Local `WalletError`: `number too large to retain precision - use readVarIntBn` |

Rows for the CLI's operator-visible table:

### Fixed: the Peer's certificate paths, nonce intake and sending bound (#445)

Both certificate paths call one validator in the reference's words
(`ts-stack@edf6e03`, `packages/sdk/src/auth/utils/validateCertificates.ts:64-137`,
called by `Peer.ts:970,1242`). Certificate responses match the locally requested
policy before validation (`Peer.ts:359-389,1229-1242`). An absent policy is the
reference's empty policy (`:154-157`), so it cannot authorize a nonempty
response. The toolbox's BRC-104 client uses this configuration; its previously
accepted unsolicited response is now refused. The e2e witness
`test_certificate_response_without_policy_is_refused` pins that change.

The intake checks every required nonce, in the reference's order
(`AuthMessageValidation.ts:64-79,355-389`), before wallet or session work.
Missing or noncanonical text is `<type>.<field> must be canonical base64.`;
canonical text of the wrong length is `<type>.<field> must encode exactly
<N> bytes.` An empty string is canonical but the wrong length. On a
certificateRequest the required-policy check follows the nonce checks; the
100-certificate bound precedes both, as in the reference.

| Message | Required nonce fields and decoded lengths, in check order |
|---|---|
| initialRequest | initialNonce: 48 |
| initialResponse | initialNonce: 48, yourNonce: 48 |
| certificateRequest | nonce: 32, initialNonce: 48, yourNonce: 48 |
| certificateResponse | nonce: 32, initialNonce: 48, yourNonce: 48 |
| general | nonce: 32, yourNonce: 48 |

This **deliberately removes the Peer's 32-byte legacy session-nonce acceptance
window introduced in 0.3.6**. Releases through 0.3.5 emitted 16 random bytes
plus a truncated 16-byte HMAC; 0.3.6 began emitting 48 bytes and kept accepting
32 for migration. Peer intake now requires 48, as the reference does. The
standalone `verify_nonce` and `validate_nonce_format` helpers retain their
legacy behavior for direct callers. Outgoing certificate requests and
responses now include the session's `initialNonce`, required by that intake.
The signer also propagates decoding failures instead of signing empty bytes.
An HTTP certificateRequest lacking initialNonce is now refused at full intake
in `certificateRequest.initialNonce must be canonical base64.`, matching the
existing #416 reference recording. Its signature witnesses supply a valid
initialNonce to reach the handler; a separate full-intake witness pins the
new refusal without altering the transport or its recorded vectors.

Certificates are judged concurrently, with the reference's mandatory promise
continuations between subject, signature/policy, and decryption results. The
Node v22.18.0 measurements with two failing certificates in both orders show:
a subject mismatch beats an invalid signature in either order; signature and
policy failures at the same stage follow array order; an invalid signature
beats a keyring-decryption failure in either order. A decryption failure
before a wallet await also beats one after a wallet await, in either order. Two subject mismatches or
two invalid signatures return the earlier array entry's words. Rust now uses
an unordered set of futures with these continuation boundaries; the wallet's
asynchronous completions decide between decryption failures, as in
`Promise.all` (`validateCertificates.ts:80-136`).

The changes in the toolbox's table, relative to the code before #445.
Certificate-fault rows assume a configured policy; the absent-policy row
names the toolbox client's configuration:

| Received or sent | Before | Now |
| certificateResponse: a certificate's subject not the sender | `Certificate subject does not match message sender` | `The subject of one of your certificates ("<subject>") is not the same as the request sender ("<sender>").` |
| certificateResponse: an unrequested certifier | `Certificate from untrusted certifier: <certifier>` | `Certificates do not match a locally requested set for this session.` |
| certificateResponse: an unrequested type | `Certificate type not in requested set: <type>` | the same match words |
| certificateResponse: a nonempty keyring revealing fewer than all requested fields | `Required field '<field>' not revealed in certificate` | accepted, as the reference accepts a nonempty subset (`validateCertificates.ts:59-62`, `Peer.ts:375-378`) |
| certificateResponse: an empty keyring, revealing no field | accepted, because the old helper skipped the field check for an empty keyring | the same match words; an empty keyring is refused (`Peer.ts:375-377`) |
| certificateResponse: a keyring revealing an unrequested field | accepted | the same match words |
| certificateResponse: nonempty certificates with no configured policy | accepted after subject and signature checks | the same match words (`Peer.ts:1239`) |
| any message with more than 100 certificates | each certificate judged | `Authentication certificates exceed their limit.` |
| send more than 100 certificates | signed and sent | `certificates must be an array of at most 100 entries`, before session lookup, signing or sending (`Peer.ts:1132-1134`) |
| a handshake nonce not canonical base64 | signed or verified over the decoded bytes, or none | the intake's canonical-base64 words |
| a 32-byte session nonce, or a later message's missing, malformed or wrong-length nonce | a 32-byte session nonce accepted (the 0.3.6 legacy window); a missing nonce refused by the Peer's own words (`General message nonce is required.`, `Certificate request message nonce is required.`, `Certificate response message nonce is required.`: the #353 and #362-364 witnesses), a malformed or wrong-length one passed intake | the intake's canonical-base64 or exact-length words above |
| a malformed initial response (a bad signature, a refused certificate, a listener error) | the handshake failed at once with the refusal | the handshake waits and returns `Handshake timeout` (`Peer.ts:1029-1035`; `tests/auth_peer_e2e_tests.rs`, test 21) |

An initial response with `certificates: []` still completes the handshake,
leaves the session waiting for required certificates, calls no certificate
listener and sends no automatic answer (`Peer.ts:845-874,961-967`). An empty
certificate response with no policy still reaches listeners. More than 100
certificates is refused at intake, ahead of any nonce or certificate
validation (`AuthMessageValidation.ts:348-352`). The validator's own bound,
`AuthMessage cannot contain more than 100 certificates.`, remains behind it.

`tests/auth_peer_certificate_paths_445.rs` pins these behaviors over in-process
transports, including 88 nonce cases and three required-policy ordering cases, both certificate paths' rejection
order, concurrent wallet decryptions, the absent policy, empty/subset/extra
keyrings and the sender's 0/100/101 boundary with and without a session. The
original handshake, empty-array, certificate-fault and receive-bound pins are
retained. `tests/support/auth_peer_certificate_paths_445.mjs` records 140
cases plus two decoder observations from an unmodified edf6e03 bundle under
Node v22.18.0, built outside the worktree. Both recordings are byte-identical;
all 18 earlier cases retain their bytes. Expected vectors are recorder output,
never hand-edited. The fold's regressions are RED on scratch 344973e7; the
empty-keyring change is RED on scratch 9a37a832, before the original #445
validator change. The public `validate_certificates` keeps its words and
rules; Peer does not call it.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#445)

The measured rejection order above is deterministic for synchronous checks;
which asynchronous wallet failure arrives earlier depends on the wallet's
completion order. Rust futures are dropped after the returned error, whereas
JavaScript's other promises may continue running. Rust keeps `AuthError` as
the error class where the reference's sender bound uses `TypeError`.
The Peer keeps no pending dynamic certificate-request policies, so only its
configured handshake policy authorizes a response (`Peer.ts:1231-1238`). An
intake-refused initial response never releases its handshake waiter: the
reference's actual 30-second wait returns `Timeout waiting for the BRC-103
initial response.` (`Peer.ts:674`), while Rust retains `Handshake timeout`.

go-sdk@2ca481c applies no 100-certificate bound (`auth/peer.go:689-720,935-966`;
`auth/utils/validate_certificates.go:143-145` refuses an empty list alone),
wraps its validator's lower-case words (`:227,273,288,304`) in
`invalid certificates: ` on the initial-response path (`auth/peer.go:716`,
`auth/errors.go:48-53`) and joins them under `ErrCertificateValidation` on the
certificate-response path (`auth/peer.go:961-963`). It refuses a nonce that
`base64.StdEncoding` cannot decode at the signer as `failed to decode initial
nonce` (`auth/peer.go:585-588`). Go was read, not executed for this fold.

### Fixed: one wallet double-spend retry for revocation and the global key-value store (#340)

The global store now retries `set` and `remove` after a wallet's structured
`WERR_REVIEW_ACTIONS` with valid double-spend evidence. Every retry follows
successful synchronization of the competing transactions and repeats the
lookup, input selection, BEEF merge and bound action. An action that failed
at signAction is aborted with its own reference before synchronization; the
next createAction supplies a new reference. The per-key lock covers every
attempt. Global set prepares its replacement script once, outside the retry,
as the reference does.

The local store does not retry, as the reference's does not. Local set makes
one bound action; local removal makes one bound action per batch and stops on
failure. The local retry and broadcaster added in the unreleased #340 change
are removed, including `LocalKVStore::with_broadcaster`. Local failures still
abort the action before returning the wallet error.

The reference rule moved from identity's private `double_spend.rs` to
`src/overlay/wallet_retry.rs`, beside the port of `overlay-tools`, where
`ts-stack@edf6e03` defines `withDoubleSpendRetry` (`:140-165`, default at `:8`).
It makes at most five attempts, synchronizes only between attempts, and returns
the final wallet error unchanged. Other errors, missing or malformed evidence,
and failed synchronization stop immediately. Identity revocation uses the
same rule with its existing error category and verdicts. The public
`overlay::with_double_spend_retry` in `retry.rs` remains a different rule:
error-text matching, three retries (four attempts) by default, and no
competing-transaction synchronization.

`tests/kvstore_double_spend_retry_340.rs` pins global set/remove recovery,
the fresh lookup's exact inputs and merged BEEF, distinct action references,
abort-before-sync order, five-attempt exhaustion in the wallet's words, and
no retry for unstructured or malformed evidence or failed synchronization.
The four local once/always set/remove cases pin one createAction, one abort,
no broadcast and the unchanged wallet error; all four fail on a scratch copy
of the retrying `dd0a4a59` tree and pass after the removal. The shared rule's
five unit tests and all nine existing `identity_revocation_checks_327`
verdict tests remain unchanged.

Migration: no published public item moved. The old identity helper was private
and the removed local `with_broadcaster` was never published.
`GlobalKVStore::with_broadcaster(TopicBroadcaster)` remains additive for
caller-owned synchronization and completed-transaction broadcasts. Existing
config struct literals are unchanged.

### Fixed: required flag reasons and the original sighash census (#453)

`ScriptFlags::check` now explains why an unsupported word is refused and
names all three required flags in each sentence. Under any supported word,
`spend/signature_encoding.rs` requires a signature's fork-ID bit and strict
encodings remain enabled; a word without these rules would be judged
differently from the node. Pre-Genesis block and UTXO rules are not implemented.
The restriction and the `Spend::validate` prefix and final period are unchanged.

| Missing flag | Old text | New text |
|---|---|---|
| SIGHASH_FORKID | `SIGHASH_FORKID is not set: this interpreter requires it in a flag word` | `SIGHASH_FORKID is not set: a word without it is not implemented by this interpreter (it requires SIGHASH_FORKID, GENESIS and UTXO_AFTER_GENESIS)` |
| GENESIS | `GENESIS is not set: this interpreter requires it in a flag word` | `GENESIS is not set: a word without it is not implemented by this interpreter (it requires SIGHASH_FORKID, GENESIS and UTXO_AFTER_GENESIS)` |
| UTXO_AFTER_GENESIS | `UTXO_AFTER_GENESIS is not set: this interpreter requires it in a flag word` | `UTXO_AFTER_GENESIS is not set: a word without it is not implemented by this interpreter (it requires SIGHASH_FORKID, GENESIS and UTXO_AFTER_GENESIS)` |

The three DER-off witnesses in `tests/script_signature_words_417.rs` and
the 86 recorded words in `tests/support/conformance_forkid_gate_429.rs` pin
the new sentences. Both tests fail with #434's old sentences in an isolated
scratch copy of `ed1093cf` with its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. The documentation
now states the reason too, and `flags.rs` remains at its 872-line ceiling.
The three stale `FORKID is always enabled here` comments in
`spend/crypto.rs` now describe both modes: a signature without the bit is
deleted from the scriptCode, including a default-mode legacy signature or
an empty signature; BIP143 applies to FORKID without CHRONICLE, and the
original digest applies otherwise. No interpreter verdict changes.

The allowlist's `legacy/OTDA sighash not implemented in bsv-rs` reason was
wrong: #22 supplied the original digest and #429 enabled signatures without
the fork-ID bit in default mode. The census only called the BIP143 preimage
API. With that class removed on a scratch copy and the existing original
digest API used, all 1,244 excluded vectors pass, zero fail and zero panic;

### Fixed: the reference's ECIES byte bounds before work (#333)

A framed envelope over the bound was read and failed on its MAC; it is now
refused in the reference's words before reading.
Both `electrum_decrypt` and `bitcore_decrypt` reject more than 16,777,376 bytes
(16 MiB plus 160) before parsing a key, deriving a secret, hashing or AES,
with `Electrum ECIES envelope must be a bounded dense byte array` or
`Bitcore ECIES envelope must be a bounded dense byte array`, respectively.
The bound is the reference's, not a caller policy: `ts-stack@edf6e03`
`packages/sdk/src/compat/ECIES.ts:12,589-594,704-709` spells the shared constant
`MAX_ECIES_ENVELOPE_BYTES` (the filing calls it `MAX_ELECTRUM_ECIES_ENVELOPE_BYTES`).
`CompatValidation.ts:1,8-15` supplies the 16 MiB base and the refusal suffix.

The encryptors also adopt the reference's 16,777,216-byte plaintext bound
before work (`ECIES.ts:551,673`, `CompatValidation.ts:1,8-15`), with
`Electrum ECIES plaintext must be a bounded dense byte array` and
`Bitcore ECIES plaintext must be a bounded dense byte array`.
These plaintext refusals use the additive `Error::EciesInvalidPlaintext` variant,
whose Display is the reference's words alone. They are validation failures before
encryption, not `EciesDecryptionFailed`; `CryptoError` would add its own prefix.
Migration: match `EciesInvalidPlaintext` for an oversized encryption input;
decrypt-side envelope refusals keep their existing variants and Display text.
The single/shared and base64 helpers inherit the Electrum bounds; the reference
defines no separate helper or base64-text bound, so none is added.
The fixed-size Bitcore IV already has the reference's 16-byte size in its Rust type.
This change left short-input, framing and MAC refusals within the limits unchanged;
#463 above updates the short-input words.

`tests/compat_ecies_bounds_333.rs` pins one byte over each limit, the exact limits,
and a framed oversized Electrum envelope (the exact cap is not a valid Electrum
frame size). It builds each large buffer once, retaining a small writer-produced
header and zero-filling the rest without computing a large envelope's MAC.
The 16 MiB plaintext round trips with and without an Electrum key and through
Bitcore. On scratch `455fe780`, five regressions were RED and three controls
passed; all eight pass with the guards. No hash-count hook exists: the guard's
length-only code path precedes every key read and hash call.
The cold-review fold pins the plaintext variant and exact Display in both
encrypt tests, including the Electrum helpers: both fail on a scratch copy with
the old `EciesDecryptionFailed` plaintext refusal, and all eight pass after it.

The encrypt-side refusal is carried by `Error::EciesInvalidPlaintext(String)`,
whose Display is the reference's words alone; no release and not this PR's base
ever printed a wrapped `ECIES decryption failed: ...` text for an encrypt call (the
plaintext bound is new in this change), so no caller matched it.

Its `BitcoreDecrypt` (`:191-214`) and both encryptors (`:62-102,157-188`)
also have no upper byte bound. Rust follows the TypeScript bounds here.
At the exact envelope cap Rust retains its existing Electrum framing error
and Bitcore MAC error; TypeScript rejects Bitcore's unaligned frame before

  `contacts_signaction_326`, `identity_wallet_calls_318` and
  `identity_revocation_checks_327` pin the identity requests.

  totals; set rejects an incomplete collapse; remove authenticates and consumes

### Fixed: internalizeAction's unreachable wire fallbacks and JSON null remittances (#393)

The two notes from #384's review are resolved. The transceiver's
`payment_remittance required for wallet payment` refusal and its empty
basket-insertion write have been removed. Its public `internalize_action`
always calls `validate_internalize_action_args` before encoding; the
`WalletClient` wire dispatch reaches that same method. No entry bypasses the
validator. `ProtoWallet`, `WalletClient` and `HttpWalletJson` also validate;
the processor still refuses internalizeAction as needing a full wallet.
`payment_remittance_guard_precedes_encoding_and_sending` and
`insertion_remittance_guard_precedes_encoding_and_sending` cover missing,
wrong-only and crossed remittances, including a payment key that would fail
hex decoding if encoding ran. Each asserts the validator's exact refusal
and zero frames sent.

A JSON `null` remittance used to become `None`, erasing its presence.
`types/internalize_output.rs` now distinguishes a missing member from null
while reading, sharing the protocol/presence check with the typed validator.
The public fields, their types and serialization stay unchanged. A null
beside the other protocol's remittance is refused with that protocol's
one-remittance words. A matching null alone reaches the object refusal,

other remittance remains accepted; an absent required one remains refused

`tests/wallet_internalize_remittance_393.rs` pins all cases in 10 tests:

reading; `two_null_remittances_are_present_and_refused_for_either_protocol`
and `a_lone_null_of_the_other_protocol_is_present_and_refused` pin the other
four null cases; the two `an_undefined_*` tests pin absence, and the two

was accepted by deserialization; the other four pass. With the transceiver's

### Fixed: out-of-scope words are not judged; live Genesis authority (#452, #451)

A pre-Genesis coin, a tip at `u32::MAX`, or a zero Genesis/Chronicle
activation set through public fields previously became `SpendRefusal::Script`
and `TransactionError("Script validation failed for input N: ...")`.
Those answers falsely judged a transaction for an unsupported era or a broken
configuration. The keeper's word of 2026-10-29 18:1xZ is implemented as
`Verdict::NotJudged { offset, txid, input, cause }` and
`SpendRefusal::NotJudged { input, cause }`, with `input: u32` and the shared
`script::NotJudgedCause`. The whole path returns
`Error::TransactionNotJudged { txid: String, input_index: usize, cause }`.
The display txid identifies the unproven transaction being checked, including
an ancestor reached by the whole-path walk. Its cause is not a resource limit
and must not inhabit `ScriptEvaluationDeclined`. New arms
are appended, preserving every existing variant's discriminant.

`NotJudgedCause` carries `PreGenesisCoin { height, genesis_height }`,
`TipHeightOverflow { tip }`, or `ZeroActivationHeight(ActivationHeightsError)`
(`ZeroGenesis` / `ZeroChronicle`). The existing pre-Genesis spend and streaming
source-height overflow refusals also retain their facts in `PreGenesisSpend`
and `SourceHeightOverflow`. The latter is reachable through synchronous
streaming `Headers`, whose heights are `u64`; the in-memory `MerklePath`
conversion and async `ChainTracker` path refuse those heights earlier.
Every diagnostic is one sentence naming the input and the bound it falls
outside, with the height where the cause has one (the zero-activation sentence
names the parameter's value, not a height).
No such refusal says that script validation failed.
The standalone `input_script_flags` API retains its error type and text, while
the live verifiers use the same checked composition with typed causes.
The whole path checks word scope before checking for a missing unlocking
script, so an out-of-scope input with no unlocking script reports `NotJudged`.

`ChainTip.genesis_height` is deprecated since `0.9.0-beta.4`. With `ChainParams`,
the params alone decide Genesis, including the stream's P2SH output check.
With no `ChainParams`, that check still reads the tip's deprecated copy,
falling back to mainnet's figure only when no tip is supplied. There are no
default-path verdict changes. The copy still functions until its removal at
the next api-break, when the default stream path judges by mainnet's heights
as the reference does with no chain parameters (the keeper's word of
2026-10-29 20:1xZ): a caller on another chain supplies its `ChainParams`, told
so by the deprecation message now and the docs then. Compatibility
constructors and the one default-path reader have scoped and explained
deprecation allowances. STN is not modelled: nothing in the stack runs there,
and the node at `879fc8b` leaves BIP65, BIP66 and CSV
heights uninitialized (`bsv-script-lean/docs/PARAMETERS.md:205`, finding #39),
so a verdict there is not reproducible. Additive support waits for a consumer
that names a use.

`tests/beef_not_judged_452.rs` pins all five causes' typed `Verdict` and
whole `Error`, with exact sentences, both zero fields, a nonzero input, no-tip cases,
synchronous/two-pass/asynchronous readers and deferred transactions. Its
`a_pre_genesis_coin_is_not_judged_by_the_stream_452`,
`an_overflowing_tip_is_not_judged_by_the_stream_452` and
`a_zero_activation_is_not_judged_by_the_stream_452` each have a matching
`*_by_the_whole_path_452` witness. The three
`beef_stream::not_judged_tests` witnesses match the actual `SpendRefusal` before
its conversion to `Verdict`. `chain_params_alone_decide_when_the_tip_disagrees_451`
pins disagreeing authorities, including the P2SH check in both directions.
`a_pre_genesis_spend_is_not_judged_452` covers a mainnet tip below 620,537
on both paths; its base-API witness is RED on the pre-#452 base with
`SpendRefused::Script` and `TransactionError`. Further witnesses name the
unproven ancestor, pin scope before a missing unlocking script, and reach
`SourceHeightOverflow` through the synchronous and two-pass stream readers.
The 13 #440 witnesses retain their decisions; their two scope refusals now
assert `NotJudged`. The word witnesses retain their verdicts. The historical
P2SH boundary witness retains its original regtest heights: a tip of 9,998
accepts the output and 9,999 refuses it with Genesis at 10,000.

**API break (`api-break`, beta line):** adding `SpendRefusal::NotJudged` extends
an exhaustive enum. Migration: downstream `match` expressions add
`SpendRefusal::NotJudged { input, cause } => ...`; `Verdict` and `Error` remain
non-exhaustive. Match typed causes for the toolbox's #461 skip and pre-Genesis
refusal, and in the CLI; never match diagnostic text. Migrate Genesis readers
to `ChainParams`; remove `ChainTip.genesis_height` initializers at the next
api-break, when the deprecated field is removed.

### Changed: arithmetic guard allocation and script-number encoding (#378, part 1)

Arithmetic guards keep their one- or two-operand metadata in stack arrays, removing
two heap allocations per arithmetic step, and inspect result-bound magnitudes only
for `OP_MUL`. Script-number encoding fills fixed slices of its pre-sized buffer,
removing a Vec growth check per limb. No arithmetic algorithm, verdict, result byte,
resource limit or public API changes.

Measured on 2026-10-29 during the 19:00 UTC hour on an Apple M1 Max, from base
`1dc611a188f2d8a61cdb2e841e5154ee6cb7d47e` in a scratch copy with its own target
directory, `cargo 1.95.0` release builds and the system allocator. Each entry is the
median-total run of three, with its own component times; seconds, Rust
**before / after**. A MiB is 1,048,576 bytes per operand. The reference is
`~/bsv/ts-stack` at `edf6e03dad39bd7bc4fc6e73e64de3a2b6f805c9`, bundled from that
revision in scratch and run via nvm's Node 22.18.0 (V8 12.4.254.21-node.27), on the
same machine in the same hour. Node's two columns are the isolated step and the
original review harness's full `Spend.validate()`; every 16 MiB run was sequential. The machine's one-minute load average was about 65 during these runs (other
lanes building), so the 16 MiB rows are load-bound: the same code gave 7.70,
12.04 and 16.37 s after the fold and 9.60, 14.16 and 18.71 s before it across
the runs, and V8's multiply 3.14 to 5.06 s.

| Operand MiB | Rust total | Decode | Multiply | Encode + push | Budget + dispatch | Node step / Spend |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.168292 / 0.118788 | 0.000956 / 0.000960 | 0.166628 / 0.117193 | 0.000698 / 0.000624 | 0.000010 / 0.000011 | 0.831143 / 0.890 |
| 4 | 2.388460 / 2.011892 | 0.005036 / 0.006089 | 2.379867 / 1.987554 | 0.003532 / 0.017669 | 0.000024 / 0.000581 | 2.414153 / 3.169 |
| 16 | 14.162800 / 12.044710 | 0.045203 / 0.022944 | 14.021576 / 12.001423 | 0.095994 / 0.020304 | 0.000027 / 0.000039 | 10.612733 / 8.450 |

The script and operands are the review's
`OP_1 <n> OP_NUM2BIN OP_INVERT OP_DUP OP_MUL OP_DROP OP_1`: two negative
numbers of magnitude `2^(8n-1)-2`. Timers bracket the actual `ScriptNum` decoder,
owned `num-bigint` multiply, result encoding and stack insertion. The remainder
includes preflight reservations, memory/length checks, dispatch, operand releases
and timer overhead. Product lengths and SHA-256 hashes match the closed-form
square and the reference at all sizes, and the final stack is `[1]`.

Attribution: decoding reads bytes directly into magnitude digits and clears the
sign bit there; moving through `BigNumber` adds no copy. Encoding still makes one
fallible, exactly sized Vec, then moves it onto the stack. `bounded_capacity` is
not on this arithmetic path. Stack budgets use stored byte counts, not a stack
walk; allocation probes reserve and release capacity without filling it. The
remaining magnitude scan is required for `OP_MUL`'s pre-allocation result bound.
The two metadata allocations were this crate's waste: a single-digit `OP_MUL`
falls from **5 allocations / 49 bytes to 3 / 17**, leaving two decoder buffers
and the result. Alternating 82 samples per encoder on already built 2, 8 and 32 MiB
results gave **0.693 / 0.623 ms, 2.787 / 2.509 ms, 14.254 / 12.056 ms**
(before / after). Those local improvements are small beside multiplication;
whole-step differences include scheduling noise and are not a claimed algorithm
speedup or a wall-clock regression threshold.

The filed **288 s versus 8.6 s** compared different instrumentation. The supplied
`review-331-fold-2/src/main.rs` installs `dhat::Alloc` and enables its heap profiler;
its Node driver has no such observer. Reusing that Rust script with active dhat
here took **147.629 s**, **147.516 s inside multiplication**, with **8,432,047
allocations / 13,640,634,303 cumulative bytes**. The ordinary release measurements
above do not reproduce 288 s; the repeat with profiling demonstrates the large
observer cost. The original 288 s sample itself was not rerun on its historical
machine state, and neither its exact latency nor a thirty-fold uninstrumented gap
is asserted by this measurement. Uninstrumented, the two are of the same order:
the cold review measured 4.43 s here against 5.07 s for the reference at 16 MiB,
and at 1 MiB this crate is about seven times faster (0.12 s against 0.83 s).

Algorithm finding: the resolved `num-bigint` is **0.4.8**, read at
`~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/num-bigint-0.4.8/src/biguint/multiplication.rs`.
For equal operands, `mac3` uses schoolbook through 32 native digits, Karatsuba
through 256, then Toom-3; unequal operands can use half-Karatsuba. All three
measured sizes enter Toom-3. Multiplication occupies **99.64%** of the
16 MiB after step. V8 bigint's public
[dispatch source](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v22.18.0/deps/v8/src/bigint/bigint-internal.cc),
[thresholds](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v22.18.0/deps/v8/src/bigint/bigint-internal.h),
and [enabled build configuration](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v22.18.0/tools/v8_gypfiles/features.gypi)
select schoolbook below 34 digits, Karatsuba below 193, Toom-Cook below 1,500,
then FFT; all these operands enter its FFT path. The installed Node binary also
contains `MultiplyFFT`, `MultiplyToomCook` and `MultiplyKaratsuba`. The gap is
size-dependent (Toom-3 against FFT at these operand sizes) and no saving figure is
claimed: the loaded runs compared one crate's multiply with another's from a
different run, and the cold review's one quiet re-measurement (load 45 to 49) put
this crate's whole 16 MiB step at 4.43 s against 5.07 s for the reference's
`Spend`. Changing the bignum dependency or adding an FFT multiply is a design
decision for the owner, not made here.

`Transaction::verify` has no work budget; `SpendParams::work_limit` and
`StreamVerifier::set_work_limit` bound charged work, while an elapsed-time bound
must be external because those counters cannot interrupt one arithmetic opcode.
The verify rustdoc and `src/transaction/CLAUDE.md` state this explicitly. Part 2 (the keeper's word of 2026-10-29 19:1xZ, on #378): `Transaction::verify`
gains an additive work budget beside the memory budget, `None` the reference's
behaviour, a spend over it not judged under #452's class with a resource cause;
a lane after this and #455 land.

The allocation ceiling is pinned by `tests/script_arithmetic_allocations_378.rs`,
and `encoding_across_limb_boundaries_keeps_the_sign_and_exact_bytes` covers both
encoder forms, signs and limb boundaries. The script witness and fixture suites
retain their expected verdicts and bytes. Measurements, raw samples, source
probes and gate/fuzz logs are under
`/Volumes/Lanes/out/bsv-rs/fix-378-op-mul-time/`; the table is the performance pin,

### Changed: HMAC tag enums are non-exhaustive before beta.4 (#443)

`HmacKeyEncoding` and `HmacVerifyPolicy` are now `#[non_exhaustive]`, so
later key encodings and verification policies can be added without breaking
callers. Both enums were introduced by #379 after v0.9.0-beta.3 was cut.
No published release carries either enum, so the change is additive in
effect.

Migration: a `match` on either enum outside the crate needs a wildcard arm
(`_ => ...`). The crate and its tests use constructors and equality checks,
with no matches on either enum needing an added arm. A test that either
enum is non-exhaustive is not expressible in Rust from inside the crate;
the pin is the rustdoc contract and the semver reading below.

Against base `1dc611a188f2d8a61cdb2e841e5154ee6cb7d47e`,
`cargo semver-checks --all-features --baseline-rev <base>` (0.51.0) assumes
a major release because both versions are `0.9.0-beta.3`, reporting
`0 checks: 0 pass, 260 skip` and `Summary no semver update required`.
Adding `--release-type minor` exercises the checks: `202 checks: 201 pass,
1 fail, 0 warn, 58 skip`. Its sole failure names `HmacKeyEncoding` and
`HmacVerifyPolicy`, with these verbatim diagnostic excerpts:

```text
--- failure enum_marked_non_exhaustive: enum marked #[non_exhaustive] ---

Description:
A public enum has been marked #[non_exhaustive]. Pattern-matching on it outside of its crate must now include a wildcard pattern like `_`, or it will fail to compile.
```

```text
     Summary semver requires new major version: 1 major and 0 minor checks failed
```

That is the expected source-compatibility finding against the unpublished
base; no other lint fails. The release-history distinction above is why
this change is additive in effect for published consumers.

### Fixed: the wallet wire's originator bound and normalization (#338)

The processor used to pass an originator through without checking its length
or hostname. It now refuses a declared length above 250 bytes before reading
the originator, with code 1 and the reference's exact words:
`Invalid originator length: expected at most 250 bytes, received N`
(`ts-stack@edf6e03`, `WalletWireProcessor.ts:286-294`, outer catch `:2379-2396`).
A named originator passes through `validate_originator` before the wallet call:
trimmed, lower-cased, and its validated port dropped. An invalid hostname is
code 6 with the validator's words. Length zero still reaches the wallet as
`None` (#329).

The transceiver used to cast the byte length to `u8`, so 256 bytes wrapped to
zero while all 256 originator bytes were sent as a malformed frame. It now
validates before constructing a frame (`WalletWireTransceiver.ts:95-100`), then
uses a checked length conversion. A 256-byte originator is refused locally as
`InvalidParameter`, `The originator parameter must be no more than 250 length.`
The words come from the shared validator, as the reference's do. No frame is
sent. Valid names are normalized before their length is written.

`wallet_wire_originator_338.rs` pins both findings:
`processor_refuses_251_bytes_in_reference_words`,
`processor_checks_length_before_reading_originator_bytes`,
`processor_accepts_250_bytes_and_normalizes_before_wallet_call`,
`processor_rejects_invalid_originator_with_reference_class`,
`transceiver_refuses_256_bytes_before_writing_any_frame`,
`transceiver_validates_named_originators_before_writing_any_frame`,
`transceiver_writes_normalized_originator_with_checked_length`, and
`empty_originators_remain_absent_on_wire`. The wire recorder
`tests/support/wire_linkage_calls_406.mjs` now accepts a third output path for
`wire_originator_338.mjs`: nine processor and nine transceiver cases recorded
from unmodified `edf6e03` under Node v22.18.0 in
`tests/vectors/wallet_wire/originator_338.json`. Its existing linkage recording
is unchanged. On an untouched scratch copy of `455fe780` with its own target
directory, seven of the eight tests fail and the empty-originator test passes;
after the fix all eight pass. `fixtures_replay` retains the in-tree wire fixtures; the external
`~/bsv/bsv-wallet-cli/tests/wire/` directory was absent at the lane's run.

Rows for the toolbox's operator-visible table (wire response codes and words):

| Trigger | Old words / behavior | New words / behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Processor receives 251 originator bytes | Passed through to the wallet | Code 1, `Invalid originator length: expected at most 250 bytes, received 251` |
| `Example.COM:8080` on either wire side | Passed through as given | Wallet receives `example.com`; transceiver writes that normalized hostname |
| Transceiver given 256 originator bytes | Wrote length 0 and all 256 bytes | `InvalidParameter`, `The originator parameter must be no more than 250 length.`; no frame |

Rows for the CLI's operator-visible table (the CLI also speaks the wire):

| Trigger | Old words / behavior | New words / behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Processor receives 251 originator bytes | Passed through to the wallet | Code 1, `Invalid originator length: expected at most 250 bytes, received 251` |
| `Example.COM:8080` on either wire side | Passed through as given | Wallet receives `example.com`; transceiver writes that normalized hostname |
| Transceiver given 256 originator bytes | Wrote length 0 and all 256 bytes | `InvalidParameter`, `The originator parameter must be no more than 250 length.`; no frame |

### Verified: handshake refusal words and signed-header order (#366, #369)

Both filings predate fixes already in base `823a798e`: #410 changed the
handshake's refusal words, and #416 moved signed-header collection to
`http/response_bounds.rs` and reused the reference collation. This entry
adds focused recorded witnesses; it changes neither runtime behavior nor
the public API.

For #366, the old `Auth endpoint returned {status}: {body}` omitted the
reference's URL, authentication explanation and bounded body preview.
`tests/support/transport_unsigned_response_354.mjs --handshake` now records
16 cases from the actual `ts-stack@edf6e03` transport under Node 22.18.0:
200 and 201 with missing headers, 300, 304, 307, 401, 404, 429 with and
without Retry-After, 500, 502, 503 with and without Retry-After, 504, and
binary/truncated previews. `transport_handshake_refusal_366.json` records
the words byte for byte, with the ephemeral server's origin as `{url}`.
The handshake does not call `#validateResponseAuthentication`; a non-2xx
uses the generic `response lacked required BSV auth headers` explanation
even when all three auth headers are present. A successful handshake needs
no auth response headers. Redirects fail in fetch before that formatter.

For #369, the filing's mixed-case/non-ASCII explanation does not apply to
the lowercased ASCII letter/digit/dash BRC-104 names. Node 22.18.0's ICU 77.1
(`en-US`, numeric false, punctuation significant) orders dash, digits, then
letters, exactly as bytes do on that set. The recorder measures all 1,407
`x-bsv-` suffixes of lengths 0 through 2 over `-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz`:
zero differing positions, identical SHA-256 of the sorted names; on letters,
digits and dash the two orders agree at any name length, not only the measured
suffixes. Raw mixed
case does differ, but the transport lowercases before collecting. HTTP
also accepts token punctuation outside that set: `x-bsv-a_` precedes
`x-bsv-a-` under localeCompare, reversing their byte order. The actual
transport accepts those names too. #416's existing collation already
handles them; changing it to a byte sort would change the signed payload.
`tests/support/transport_header_collation_369.mjs` records three full
response payloads, their included headers, the measurement and rejected
non-ASCII names in `transport_header_collation_369.json`.

Pinned by `tests/transport_handshake_refusal_366.rs` (four tests) and
`tests/transport_header_collation_369.rs` (three tests), using wiremock
ephemeral ports. The requested base already passes. RED was therefore
measured by restoring only the historical sentence and byte sort in a
scratch copy with its own target directory: the two refusal tests and
the wider HTTP-token payload test fail their equality assertions; four
other tests still pass. All seven pass with the base's fixes retained.
Both new vectors and #354's unchanged 22-case vector are byte-identical
on recorder re-run. No production function or file grew.

Downstream matching table (the historical text was replaced by #410, whose
entry carries the change; no downstream files changed):

| Site | Old | New / finding |
| Handshake refusal | `Auth endpoint returned {status}: {body}` | `Received HTTP {status} {reason} from {url}/.well-known/auth without valid BSV authentication (response lacked required BSV auth headers)` plus ` - body preview: {preview}` for a nonempty body |
| `~/bsv/rust-message-box/src/` | Exact old sentence/prefix searched | No matching sites |
| `~/bsv/bsv-middleware-cloudflare-public/src/` | Exact old sentence/prefix search attempted | Checkout absent; downstream sites unverified |

### Fixed: spend every current key-value token (#343)

`GlobalKVStore::set` now requests token data for the exact key, controller and
protocol namespace, merges every authenticated token's BEEF and spends each
outpoint once when creating its replacement. `remove` uses the same selection
and spends the whole set. Both paths use a PushDrop unlocker for each outpoint,
with its own source script and satoshis, mapped to the wallet's returned input
index. The #341/#342 request and signed-result checks, abort behavior and
`acceptDelayedBroadcast`, `randomizeOutputs`, `noSend` and `sendWith` options
remain in place. Previously global set requested no token data, removal used
one token, and both stores supplied empty unlocking scripts.

The global writer now emits the reference's JSON protocol and derives its
locking key and signature from that protocol and the stored key, so its new
tokens can be spent by those unlockers. Global mutation lookups send
`protocolID: [1, namespace]` and exclude tokens outside that authenticated
namespace. The local store already selected all listed outputs on update and
removal; it now signs each, and its same-value shortcut applies only when one
output remains. Two outputs with the same value are collapsed too.

`tests/kvstore_tokens_343.rs` has eleven recording-wallet regressions: two
current tokens on both stores' set/remove paths, reversed wallet input order,
merged BEEF, executable signatures with unequal satoshis and nonzero output
indexes, a single-token control, same-value collapse, namespace/controller and
signature filtering, repeated lookup outpoints, and the reference writer and
query shapes. On a scratch copy of `823a798e` with a separate target directory,
ten tests fail and the unchanged single-token local value passes. The #326,
#341/#342 and #344 vectors regenerate byte-identically under Node 22.18.0 at
`ts-stack@edf6e03`; no recorder or vector was changed.

Migration: no public Rust API changes. A same-value local write now spends
multiple current outputs. Pre-#343 raw-protocol global tokens remain readable,
but are outside the reference's authenticated mutation namespace; recovery of
those old identity-key-locked outputs requires their owner's wallet.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity (#343)

This follows `ts-stack@edf6e03` `GlobalKVStore.ts:343-380` (all update inputs,
merged BEEF and per-outpoint unlockers), `:431-470` (all removal inputs), and
`LocalKVStore.ts:377-425,456-537,567-594` (all authenticated outputs, and the
single-output unchanged-value shortcut). Go at `2ca481c` has only a local
store: `kvstore/local_kv_store.go:284-345,429-497` iterates all listed outpoints
for both operations and uses their BEEF and PushDrop signers, but its
same-value shortcut at `:243-245` accepts multiple outputs too. Go has no
global store. Rust's existing local lookup authentication/pagination and global
double-spend retry differences are not addressed by this change.

Seven differences from the reference stand in this change, found by its cold
review and stated here (CLAUDE.md rule 1): the unlocker signs over the source
output inside the wallet's signable transaction (`token_spends.rs:108-117`),
where the reference signs over the token's own satoshis and locking script
(`GlobalKVStore.ts:359-360`, `LocalKVStore.ts:403-404,505-506`); one input per

token, repeats included (`GlobalKVStore.ts:343-347`); the `protocolId` rewrite
to `protocolID:[1,name]` (`global_actions.rs:190-199`) applies to every global
lookup, the public `query()` with `with_protocol_id` included, not the mutation
lookups alone; the local `remove` now takes the key lock (`local.rs:279`), as
the reference does (`LocalKVStore.ts:569`); the input description and unlocking
length are now the reference's (74 bytes, `Previous KVStore token` and `KVStore
token to remove`) where they were 107 and `KV entry input`; `token_lock` calls
createSignature before getPublicKey and after the lookup, where the reference
calls getPublicKey (`PushDrop.ts:155`) then createSignature (`:175`), both
before the lookup (`GlobalKVStore.ts:298` before `:309`); and the controller
match is exact, where the reference lower-cases both sides
(`GlobalKVStore.ts:666-668`). The signature request shape (`hashToDirectlySign`
here, `data: sha256(preimage)` in the reference's `PushDrop.ts:246-248`) is
crate-wide and older than this change; it and the local lookup pagination gap
(`LocalKVStore.ts:332-339,574-590`) are filed as follow-ups.

### Added: typed wallet faults and stored abort acceptance (#439)

Under the owner's 20.4 (a) word of 2026-10-29 through the keeper, add
`WalletFaultFamily::{Transport, Service, Storage, Internal}`, `WalletFault`
and `AbortAcceptance`, with `Error::WalletFault` and `Error::AbortAccepted`.
The types are available under `error` and at the crate root with `wallet`.
Hosts can classify faults and select the stored-acceptance recovery hint by
matching typed data instead of parsing messages.

`WalletFault::new(family, message)` retains the original string:
`Error::WalletFault(f).to_string() == Error::WalletError(f.message.clone()).to_string()`.
The legacy `WalletError(String)` and its `wallet error: ` prefix are unchanged.
`AbortAcceptance::new(reference, class, message)` retains the guard's full
string and reference refusal class. Its presence affirms stored acceptance;
optional `txid`, `status` and `accepting_word` carry the context the guard
knows. The toolbox wraps it as
`Error::AbortAccepted(Box::new(AbortAcceptance::new(reference, class, message)))`,
or fills the optional fields before boxing the record. Boxing the variant
keeps `Error` at its pre-change size (56 bytes on 64-bit targets).
Both the record and `Error::AbortAccepted` display the guard's string
exactly, as `WalletRefusal { class, message }` does. This distinguishes the
status guard's `InvalidParameter` from the shared guard's `InvalidOperation`
without changing either judgement. It describes a refused abort, not a
successful abort or a chain proof, and does not cover retirement guards.

An accepted-abort refusal travels on the wire as its class's code and words,
exactly as the corresponding `WalletRefusal`; the typed record is a Rust-side
reading, with no new wire fields. Classes with an SDK wire code retain it
and the message (2 to 8, including `InvalidParameter` at 6). Classes without
one follow the existing `Wallet operation failed`, code 1 rule, including
`InvalidOperation`. `WalletFault` frames exactly as `WalletError` does.

No existing producer emits either new variant. The toolbox will supply the
metadata on its own lane; no wallet, refusal, transport or wire verdict
changes here. `tests/wallet_fault_439.rs` pins the four families and both
acceptance guards in five tests: display bytes, typed fields, equality and
cloning. The same tests do not compile on the base because the types and
variants do not exist. `tests/wallet_fault_wire_439.rs` checks all twenty
classes against their legacy frames, all four fault families against
`WalletError`, and the 64-bit enum size. The frame and size regressions fail
on the unboxed, pre-fold record. The preceding room-making commit moves
`WalletRefusalClass` and its impls byte for byte with a re-export at the old
path; its twenty classes are unchanged.

Migration: additive. Existing matches with a fallback keep working; hosts
may match the new variants when their toolbox supplies them.

These types are the port's extension beyond the reference, not a parity
item or a divergence: `ts-stack@edf6e03`'s
`packages/sdk/src/wallet/WalletError.ts` has a string and a code, with no
fault family or acceptance record. The string remains the reference's,
byte for byte. The reference's twenty refusal classes remain its own.

### Added: the node's per-input script word from chain facts (#440)

The keeper's rule (RULINGS-2026-10-12.md, 2026-10-28 16:5xZ, corrected at
22:0xZ, with the 2026-10-29 10:5xZ no-tip clause and 16:0xZ shape): “a door
that judges a transaction for a wallet, a topic or a tracker runs the interpreter
under the node's word”, “two words combined per input”. Transaction flags come
from the spend height (tip + 1 unmined, containing block height mined); the coin's
two UTXO bits come from its verified BUMP height, or the spend era if unproven.
Without a mining tip the latest era the chain constants know applies. SDK default
mode remains the reference's parity mode, never the live-door selection.

The existing non-exhaustive `block::ChainParams` now carries `genesis_height`
and `chronicle_height`: mainnet 620538 / 943816, testnet 1344302 / 1713168,
regtest 10000 / 15000 (`bitcoin-sv@879fc8b src/chainparams.cpp:18,23;20,25;21,26`).
`mainnet()` and `testnet()` join the existing `main()`, `test()` and `regtest()`;
test-network overrides use `chain.with_activation_heights(genesis, chronicle)`.
The fields stay public. These match `-genesisactivationheight` and
`-chronicleactivationheight` (`bitcoin-sv@879fc8b src/init.cpp:2473-2481`).
Zero is refused for either field by the shared activation check, including
when `input_script_flags` receives public fields mutated by a caller, as the
node refuses zero or negative heights (`configscriptpolicy.cpp:310-321,353-364`);
negative heights are unrepresentable as `u32`. The constructor returns
`ActivationHeightsError`; the composition function maps the same refusal and
node sentence to `ScriptFlagsError::NotApplicable`, because an unusable chain
configuration cannot select a script word. Teranode's regtest uses 100 / 200
(`go-chaincfg` v1.6.2 `params.go:475-476`), so its fixtures use
`ChainParams::regtest().with_activation_heights(100, 200)?`. Activation parameters
stand separately from the moving `ChainTip` header facts.

`script::input_script_flags(&chain, spend_height, source_proven_height, mined)`
computes the word in one place. It follows the sibling
`bsv-script-lean/docs/PARAMETERS.md:103,123,125,168` and the node's
`policy/policy.h:226-245`, `validation.cpp:2973-2982`,
`protocol_era.cpp:21-39` at `879fc8b`. Both UTXO bits are replaced with the
coin's bits; transaction CHRONICLE remains the spend's. A pre-Genesis coin or
spend is refused with an explicit unsupported-era sentence, never silently
PostGenesis. The interpreter still does not model pre-Genesis coins; this refusal
is an API limitation, not a node consensus verdict that such coins are invalid.

`StreamVerifier::with_chain_params` (also async),
`verify_stream_two_pass_with_chain_params`, and
`Transaction::verify_with_chain_params` are additive. They apply the computed
word before each `Spend::validate`; scripts share the existing per-transaction
sighash cache. The retaining reader still keeps only referenced output scripts.
Structural, atomic, mining-context, value, resource-decline, duplicate-entry and
deferred-parent behavior is unchanged. Proven transactions still stop at the
proof; the standalone function's `mined` argument serves callers judging mined
scripts. The builder is local configuration, reapplied after any cursor resume,
as the budgets are. Existing APIs retain default evaluation and their signatures.

This serves the toolbox's #422/#432, the engine's #205 and the storage server's
`tracker_rule.rs:48-68`, replacing each caller's word composition. Unit tests pin
network constants and numeric same-era/mixed-era words at Genesis and Chronicle.
The unit tests `a_zero_genesis_activation_height_is_refused` and
`a_zero_chronicle_activation_height_is_refused` pin public-field and constructor
refusals; removing the shared zero checks makes both fail with a post-Chronicle
word where the refusal belongs.
`tests/beef_stream_word_440.rs` builds signed BEEFs for the 0x01 FORKID refusal,
version-1 0x61 acceptance across a mixed-era boundary and refusal before Chronicle,
OP_SUBSTR, unproven/pre-Genesis/no-tip cases, each input's height, deferred and
resumed readers and resource declines. The existing four word witness files stay
unchanged. No fixture recordings were added. Migration: none; additive.

### Notes: cross-SDK parity

`@bsv/sdk` at `ts-stack@edf6e03` has no chain-parameter object or automatic
per-input word derivation in its default `Transaction.verify` path: it builds
`Spend` without flags and runs its default mode
(`packages/sdk/src/transaction/Transaction.ts:1391-1456`). `Spend` can accept
explicit flags (`packages/sdk/src/script/Spend.ts:275-304`); that does not select
the caller's network or activation heights. The toolbox's verifier is a caller
that supplies height context (`packages/wallet/wallet-toolbox/src/signer/methods/verifyUnlockScripts.ts:329-350,384`).
This crate's chain-parameter path is an additive live-door API; the existing
verification APIs retain the SDK default mode.

Go supplies activation heights from the verifier's tracker or caller
(`go-sdk@2ca481c spv/script_flags.go:15-36,51-57`) and passes its per-input word
to the interpreter (`spv/verify.go:537-549`), using
`script/interpreter/scriptflag/heights.go:44-90`, and differs in three ways:
its `spv.Verify` works the word out itself, with mainnet heights when the
tracker names no network (`spv/script_flags.go:53-57`); it judges an unmined
transaction under the block word with the heights at `MaxUint32`
(`spv/verify.go:537-549`, `heights.go:52`), where this crate uses the standard
word at tip plus one as the node does (`validation.cpp:1032`); and it treats
an unproven P2SH-shaped coin as pre-Genesis (`verify.go:563-575`), where this
crate refuses a pre-Genesis coin. Its zero-valued activation fields make the
rules active from the start (`heights.go:3-16`); this crate instead follows
the SV node's refusal of zero. Pre-Genesis interpretation remains unsupported
here, as described above.
